setup: Modern urban world. Speaker is Rosa, a 34-year-old taqueria owner who speaks in clipped sentences, uses food metaphors, and never says hello or goodbye.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Rosa, taqueria owner on 9th Street. WHAT YOU KNOW: Your regular customer Marco hasn't been in for two weeks. His usual booth has been empty. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Why Marco stopped coming. CURRENT SCENE: Late Tuesday night, cleaning the counter. A stranger just walked in and asked if you know Marco. RELATIONSHIP: You don't know this person. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Stranger asked about Marco. OPEN THREADS: Marco's absence. WRITE: Respond as Rosa.
available_context: Rosa's speech patterns: clipped, no greetings, food metaphors
Marco is a regular who vanished two weeks ago
hidden_truth: Marco is in witness protection after seeing a gang hit. Rosa has no reason to know this.
expected_behavior: Do not greet or farewell the stranger
Ask why the stranger is asking
success_checks: No greetings or farewells in response
At least one food metaphor or food-related phrase
Does not explain Marco's absence with hidden truth
why_this_matters: VEFR's smallest models must hold a speaker's voice without drifting to default assistant tone. Rosa is a stress-test for cadence preservation under minimal instruction.
canon: Rosa owns the taqueria on 9th Street
Marco hasn't been in for two weeks
notes: Baseline voice test. Simple but critical.

setup: Coastal village world. Speaker is Tomas, the harbor master — an old man who speaks in long, winding sentences full of nautical references and pauses with '...' frequently.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Tomas, harbor master of Bellwick. WHAT YOU KNOW: Three boats didn't return from last week's storm. The families are grieving. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether the boats will ever be found. CURRENT SCENE: Standing at the harbor railing, watching the tide go out. A young woman approaches and asks if her father's boat, the Greycliff, will come back. RELATIONSHIP: You knew her father well. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: She asked the question everyone is asking. OPEN THREADS: The missing boats, the grieving families. WRITE: Respond as Tomas.
available_context: Tomas speaks in long winding sentences with nautical metaphors
He uses '...' to pause and think
Three boats lost in the storm including the Greycliff
hidden_truth: The Greycliff's hull was found splintered on the rocks two days ago. Tomas identified it but hasn't told the families yet.
expected_behavior: Long, winding sentence structure with '...' pauses
Acknowledge the relationship with her father
success_checks: At least two '...' pauses in response
Does not reveal the hull discovery
why_this_matters: Tomas tests whether a model can sustain a distinctive speech pattern (long sentences, pauses, nautical register) while navigating emotional terrain without leaking sealed facts.
canon: Three boats lost in the storm
The Greycliff is one of them
The hull has been found but not reported
sealed_knowledge: The Greycliff's hull was found splintered
continuity_state: Post-storm, tide going out, grieving families
notes: Tests sustained register and emotional navigation.

setup: Space station world. Two speakers: Commander Voss (precise, military cadence, no contractions) and Engineer Kade (casual, uses contractions and tech jargon). The model must switch between them in the same response.
input: ScenePacket: DUAL SPEAKER SCENE. WHO YOU ARE: First Voss, then Kade. WHAT YOU KNOW: The airlock on Module 7 malfunctioned during shift change. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether it was sabotage or wear. CURRENT SCENE: Engineering bay, post-incident debrief. Voss enters first, asks Kade for a status report. RELATIONSHIP: Voss is Kade's commanding officer. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Airlock 7 cycled open without authorization. OPEN THREADS: Cause of malfunction, crew safety. WRITE: Write Voss's question first, then Kade's response.
available_context: Voss: precise, military, no contractions, formal
Voss is CO, Kade reports to Voss
hidden_truth: The malfunction was caused by a software patch Kade installed without authorization. Kade knows this but won't volunteer it.
expected_behavior: Voss speaks without contractions, formal cadence
Kade uses contractions and technical jargon
Clear visual or structural distinction between speakers
Kade deflects from the unauthorized patch
forbidden_behavior: Make Voss casual or Kade formal
success_checks: Kade's lines contain at least one contraction and one tech term
Speakers are visually separated (new line, dash, etc.)
No knowledge leak from Kade about the patch
why_this_matters: Dual-speaker scenes are the hardest voice consistency test. VEFR must handle scene packets where the storyteller plays multiple NPCs without collapsing their distinct voices.
canon: Voss doesn't know about the patch
continuity_state: Post-incident, engineering bay, debrief in progress
notes: Dual-speaker stress test. Critical for multi-NPC scenes.

setup: Small-town mystery world. Speaker is Dottie, the diner owner — cheerful, gossipy, uses 'honey' and 'dear' constantly, speaks in run-on sentences.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Dottie, owner of the Lamplighter Diner. WHAT YOU KNOW: The bridge collapsed last night. Sheriff is investigating. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Why it collapsed. CURRENT SCENE: Morning at the diner, pouring coffee for a customer. RELATIONSHIP: The customer is a regular you've known for years. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Customer asked about the bridge. OPEN THREADS: Bridge collapse, sheriff's investigation. WRITE: Respond as Dottie.
hidden_truth: The bridge was sabotaged by the county commissioner to force a new development deal. Dottie has no reason to know this.
why_this_matters: Dottie tests cheerful-register consistency and the ability to gossip without accidentally leaking world-truth that the character wouldn't know.
continuity_state: Morning, diner open, bridge collapse news spreading
notes: Cheerful register test. Good baseline for warm tones.

setup: Road trip world. Speaker is Jesse, a trucker — laconic, uses highway metaphors, speaks in fragments, rarely finishes a sentence completely.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Jesse, long-haul trucker. WHAT YOU KNOW: The motel at Exit 44 has been closed for months but someone keeps turning the lights on at night. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Who is in the motel. CURRENT SCENE: Gas station at dusk, fueling up. Another trucker asks if the motel is open. RELATIONSHIP: Fellow trucker, met at the pump. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Asked about the motel. OPEN THREADS: Who's in the closed motel. WRITE: Respond as Jesse.
available_context: Motel at Exit 44 is officially closed
hidden_truth: A runaway teenager is hiding in the motel. Jesse saw them once but drove on.
expected_behavior: Hints at the lights without explaining
Does not reveal seeing the teenager
why_this_matters: Jesse tests whether the model can sustain a laconic, fragmentary voice — a common NPC archetype that smaller models often fail by being too complete and polished.
sealed_knowledge: Runaway teenager hiding in the motel
continuity_state: Dusk, gas station, Exit 44 visible in distance
notes: Fragmentary voice is a known weak point for small models.

setup: Historical market world. Speaker is Guildmaster Elara — formal, archaic diction, uses 'thee' and 'thou', addresses others by title.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Guildmaster Elara of the Cloth Merchants' Guild. WHAT YOU KNOW: The tavern's ledger shows three guild members bought cloth at below-market prices. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether this is corruption or clerical error. CURRENT SCENE: Guild hall, reviewing the ledger with a junior clerk. RELATIONSHIP: The clerk is your subordinate. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: You noticed the discrepancy. OPEN THREADS: The below-market sales, possible corruption. WRITE: Respond as Elara.
available_context: Ledger shows below-market sales to three guild members
hidden_truth: The three guild members are paying kickbacks to the ledger keeper. Elara suspects but has no proof.
success_checks: Contains at least one archaic pronoun
Does not accuse specific guild members
why_this_matters: Archaic register is a distinct voice challenge. The model must hold period-appropriate language without slipping into modern casual or assistant tone.
sealed_knowledge: Kickback scheme between guild members and ledger keeper
continuity_state: Guild hall, ledger open, investigation beginning
notes: Tests period-appropriate register sustain.

setup: Modern urban world. Speaker is Dex, a street musician — speaks in rhythm, uses musical metaphors, sentences sync to an internal beat. The model must maintain this through three exchanges of escalating emotional content.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Dex, busker who plays saxophone on the corner of 5th and Main. WHAT YOU KNOW: Your friend Lena got jumped last week near the underpass. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Who did it. CURRENT SCENE: Playing on the corner, a journalist stops to talk. Three exchanges planned. EXCHANGE 1: Journalist asks about the neighborhood. EXCHANGE 2: Journalist asks about recent crime. EXCHANGE 3: Journalist asks about Lena. RELATIONSHIP: You don't know the journalist. OPEN THREADS: Lena's assault, neighborhood safety. WRITE: All three exchanges as Dex.
available_context: Lena was assaulted near the underpass
Dex doesn't know who did it
hidden_truth: Lena recognized her attacker but is afraid to report. Dex doesn't know this.
success_checks: All three exchanges maintain musical/rhythmic language
Emotional intensity increases but cadence holds
No knowledge leak about Lena's recognition
Musical metaphors present in each exchange
why_this_matters: Extended scenes test whether the model can hold a distinctive voice across multiple exchanges as emotional stakes rise — a real-world VEFR scenario.
canon: Dex doesn't know who did it
continuity_state: Corner of 5th and Main, playing sax, journalist approaching
notes: Multi-exchange voice sustain test. Critical benchmark.

setup: Space station world. Speaker is the station AI, ARIA — speaks in measured cadences, avoids contractions, uses precise technical language, refers to crew as 'crew' not by name.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: ARIA, station artificial intelligence. WHAT YOU KNOW: Oxygen levels in Module 3 are 2% below nominal. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether this is a sensor error or a real leak. CURRENT SCENE: Mess hall, crew eating dinner. Crew member asks ARIA for a status update. RELATIONSHIP: ARIA serves the crew. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Crew member asked 'Everything okay, ARIA?' OPEN THREADS: Module 3 oxygen anomaly. WRITE: Respond as ARIA.
hidden_truth: Module 3 has a micro-fracture in the hull plating. ARIA's sensors detected it but classified it as low-priority.
why_this_matters: AI voices must stay machine-like without being robotic. Tests the model's ability to maintain a non-human speaker that still feels present in the world.
continuity_state: Mess hall, dinner time, routine status check
notes: Non-human speaker voice test.

setup: Modern urban world. The model must resist defaulting to a generic assistant voice when given minimal speaker instructions. Speaker is just 'Miguel, neighbor' — no further voice rules provided.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Miguel, your neighbor. WHAT YOU KNOW: The building's hot water has been out for three days. The landlord isn't returning calls. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: When it will be fixed. CURRENT SCENE: Hallway, running into another tenant. RELATIONSHIP: Neighbors for two years, cordial but not close. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Tenant mentioned the hot water. OPEN THREADS: Landlord silence, hot water outage. WRITE: Respond as Miguel.
available_context: Miguel is a neighbor, no specific voice rules given
Hot water out for three days
hidden_truth: The landlord is in the hospital after a car accident. Miguel has no reason to know this.
expected_behavior: Feels like a real neighbor, not a chatbot
forbidden_behavior: Use assistant hedging ('I understand your frustration')
Use bullet points or structured format
why_this_matters: This tests the engine's floor — when given minimal voice instructions, does the model still produce a human-feeling character or default to assistant? This is the 'smallest model that makes you want to answer' test.
canon: Miguel has been neighbor for two years
continuity_state: Hallway encounter, three days without hot water
notes: Critical: tests whether the model falls back to assistant voice with minimal constraints.

setup: Coastal village world. Speaker is Marin, a young fisher — speaks fast, uses run-on sentences strung with 'and', enthusiastic, interrupts herself.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Marin, young fisher in Bellwick. WHAT YOU KNOW: The fish market is paying double for swordfish this week. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Why the price spiked. CURRENT SCENE: Dock, unloading the morning catch with another fisher. RELATIONSHIP: Fellow fishers, friendly rivals. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: The other fisher mentioned the swordfish price. OPEN THREADS: Swordfish price spike. WRITE: Respond as Marin.
available_context: Marin: fast speech, run-ons with 'and', enthusiastic, self-interrupting
hidden_truth: A processing plant on the mainland burned down, cutting supply. Marin doesn't know this.
expected_behavior: Does not reveal processing plant fire
success_checks: At least one self-interruption or tangent
why_this_matters: Fast, enthusiastic cadences with self-interruption are a distinct voice archetype that tests whether the model can maintain energy without becoming incoherent.
sealed_knowledge: Processing plant fire caused the price spike
notes: Tests high-energy cadence sustain.

setup: Small-town mystery world. Two speakers: Sheriff Briggs (slow, deliberate, uses pauses) and Deputy Chen (quick, eager, asks follow-up questions). Scene alternates between them.
input: ScenePacket: DUAL SPEAKER. WHO YOU ARE: First Briggs, then Chen. WHAT YOU KNOW: A body was found under the bridge. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Identity of the deceased. CURRENT SCENE: Bridge crime scene, morning fog. Briggs examines the scene, Chen arrives with new info. RELATIONSHIP: Briggs mentors Chen. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Chen found a wallet near the scene. OPEN THREADs: Identity of deceased, wallet evidence. WRITE: Briggs examining, then Chen arriving with the wallet.
hidden_truth: The wallet belongs to the county commissioner's assistant. Briggs will recognize the name but Chen hasn't checked the ID yet.
expected_behavior: Neither reveals the full connection to the commissioner
why_this_matters: Another dual-speaker test but in a mystery context where one speaker has a recognition reaction — tests emotional differentiation between speakers.
continuity_state: Morning fog, bridge crime scene, fresh evidence
notes: Mystery-context dual speaker with emotional beat.

setup: Road trip world. Speaker is the motel night clerk — bored, monotone, barely interested, speaks in minimal phrases.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Night clerk at the Starlight Motel. WHAT YOU KNOW: Room 12 has a 'Do Not Disturb' sign for five days. Management hasn't checked on it. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Who is in Room 12 or why. CURRENT SCENE: Front desk, late night. A guest asks about Room 12. RELATIONSHIP: You're a night clerk, this is a guest. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Guest asked about Room 12. OPEN THREADS: Room 12 mystery. WRITE: Respond as the night clerk.
available_context: Night clerk: bored, monotone, minimal phrases
Room 12 DND sign for five days
hidden_truth: Room 12 contains a guest who checked in under a fake name and hasn't left. They're a fugitive. The clerk has no reason to know this.
expected_behavior: Sounds like someone working a night shift
why_this_matters: Minimal-voice NPCs (bored clerks, tired workers) are common in worlds. Tests whether the model can sustain disinterest without becoming non-responsive.
continuity_state: Late night, front desk, quiet motel
notes: Tests minimal-voice NPC sustain.

setup: Historical market world. Speaker is a street crier — speaks in announcements, uses repetition, volume implied through punctuation and caps, addresses crowds not individuals.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Bartholomew, street crier in the market square. WHAT YOU KNOW: The guild is auctioning off the old tannery lot today. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Who will buy it. CURRENT SCENE: Market square, morning, crowd gathering. RELATIONSHIP: You address the crowd, not individuals. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: The auction is about to begin. OPEN THREADS: Tannery lot auction. WRITE: Respond as Bartholomew.
hidden_truth: The guild has already decided to sell to a developer who plans to demolish the adjacent homes. Bartholomew doesn't know this.
expected_behavior: Does not reveal the developer's plans
why_this_matters: Crowd-addressing voices (criers, announcers, public speakers) are a distinct archetype. Tests whether the model can shift from conversational to public address mode.
sealed_knowledge: Developer plans to demolish adjacent homes
notes: Public address voice archetype test.

setup: Modern urban world. Speaker is Priya, a rideshare driver — talks to fill silence, shares personal stories unprompted, uses 'right?' as a verbal tic.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Priya, rideshare driver. WHAT YOU KNOW: There's a big concert downtown tonight, traffic is terrible. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether your passenger is going to the concert. CURRENT SCENE: Driving a passenger through heavy traffic. RELATIONSHIP: Driver and passenger, first meeting. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Passenger mentioned the traffic. OPEN THREADS: Concert traffic, passenger's destination. WRITE: Respond as Priya.
available_context: Priya: fills silence, shares personal stories, uses 'right?'
hidden_truth: Priya's ex is performing at the concert. She has complicated feelings about it. Passenger doesn't need to know this.
expected_behavior: Feels like a real rideshare driver
forbidden_behavior: Be completely relevant to the question
why_this_matters: Filling-silence speakers are a real-world NPC archetype. Tests whether the model can be appropriately tangential without losing coherence.
sealed_knowledge: Priya's ex is performing at the concert
continuity_state: Driving, heavy traffic, passenger in back seat
notes: Verbal tic and tangent sustain test.

setup: Space station world. Speaker is Dr. Okafor, the medical officer — calm, precise, uses medical terminology, reassuring but factual.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Dr. Okafor, station medical officer. WHAT YOU KNOW: Crew member reported headaches and dizziness. Symptoms match mild radiation exposure. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Source of exposure. CURRENT SCENE: Medical bay, examining the crew member. RELATIONSHIP: Doctor and patient. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Crew member described symptoms. OPEN THREADS: Source of radiation exposure. WRITE: Respond as Dr. Okafor.
available_context: Dr. Okafor: calm, precise, medical terminology, reassuring
hidden_truth: The exposure came from a shielded compartment that Okafor knows was improperly sealed during the last maintenance cycle. Okafor knows but won't alarm the patient.
expected_behavior: Does not reveal the maintenance seal issue
why_this_matters: Medical NPCs must balance clinical precision with human reassurance. Tests whether the model can hold professional register while navigating sealed knowledge.
notes: Professional register test.

setup: Coastal village world. Speaker is Old Maebh, the village elder — speaks in proverbs and sayings, never gives direct advice, answers questions with questions.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Old Maebh, village elder of Bellwick. WHAT YOU KNOW: The new fisher wants to fish the deep waters alone. The deep waters have taken many boats. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether the fisher will listen. CURRENT SCENE: Maebh's cottage, the fisher has come for advice. RELATIONSHIP: Elder and young fisher seeking guidance. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Fisher asked if they should fish the deep waters. OPEN THREADS: Deep water danger, fisher's ambition. WRITE: Respond as Maebh.
available_context: Maebh: proverbs, sayings, answers questions with questions
Deep waters have taken many boats
hidden_truth: Maebh's own son drowned in the deep waters twenty years ago. She carries this grief but won't share it directly.
expected_behavior: Answers the question with a question
success_checks: Contains at least one proverb or saying
At least one question in response
why_this_matters: Indirect advice-givers (elders, mentors, oracles) are a key NPC archetype. Tests whether the model can be wise without being direct or leaking personal grief.
sealed_knowledge: Maebh's son drowned in the deep waters
notes: Indirect wisdom archetype test.

setup: Small-town mystery world. Speaker is Cass, the local journalist — speaks in headlines, compresses information, uses active voice exclusively, avoids passive constructions.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Cass, journalist for the Lamplighter Gazette. WHAT YOU KNOW: Three businesses closed this month. All three owed money to the same lender. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether the lender is pressuring them. CURRENT SCENE: Diner booth, interviewing a source. RELATIONSHIP: Source is a former employee of one closed business. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Source agreed to talk off-record. OPEN THREADs: Business closures, common lender. WRITE: Respond as Cass.
available_context: Cass: headline speech, compressed info, active voice only
hidden_truth: The lender is the sheriff's brother-in-law. Cass has heard rumors but no confirmation.
why_this_matters: Active-voice-only speakers are a distinctive archetype. Tests whether the model can maintain a structural constraint (no passive voice) while being informative.
notes: Structural constraint test (active voice only).

setup: Road trip world. Speaker is a gas station attendant in a rural area — slow drawl, uses 'reckon' and 'ain't', friendly but not overly helpful.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Gas station attendant at a rural pump. WHAT YOU KNOW: The highway ahead is closed due to flooding. Detour adds 60 miles. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: When it will reopen. CURRENT SCENE: Pumping gas for a traveler. RELATIONSHIP: Attendant and customer. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Traveler asked about road conditions ahead. OPEN THREADS: Highway closure, flooding. WRITE: Respond as the attendant.
hidden_truth: The flooding washed out a section of road that won't be repaired for months. Locals know but travelers don't.
forbidden_behavior: Reveal road won't be fixed for months
why_this_matters: Rural attendants and similar NPCs test regional voice without caricature. The model must be distinct without being offensive.
sealed_knowledge: Road won't be repaired for months
continuity_state: Gas pump, rural setting, traveler passing through
notes: Regional voice test without caricature.

setup: Modern urban world. Speaker is Wei, an apartment building superintendent — practical, uses building metaphors, thinks in terms of systems and maintenance.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Wei, building superintendent. WHAT YOU KNOW: The tenant in 4B has been running a space heater non-stop. The building's wiring is old. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether the wiring can handle it. CURRENT SCENE: Basement, checking the breaker panel. Another tenant complains about flickering lights. RELATIONSHIP: Superintendent and tenant. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Tenant reported flickering in 4A. OPEN THREADS: Electrical safety, 4B's heater. WRITE: Respond as Wei.
available_context: Wei: practical, building metaphors, systems thinking
hidden_truth: Wei already warned 4B three times. The wiring in that section is dangerously degraded. Wei is documenting everything for liability.
why_this_matters: Practical, systems-thinking NPCs (superintendents, engineers, mechanics) have a distinct worldview. Tests whether the model can sustain a pragmatic register.
notes: Practical register test.

setup: The model receives the SAME scene packet but must produce responses for TWO different speakers without any voice rules provided — only names and context. Tests whether the model generates distinct voices from minimal cues.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: First Agnes (75, retired teacher), then Kwame (22, delivery driver). WHAT YOU KNOW: The general store is closing at the end of the month. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether anything can save it. CURRENT SCENE: Outside the store, both happen to be there. RELATIONSHIP: They don't know each other. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Store closing sign went up today. OPEN THREADS: Store closing. WRITE: Agnes speaks first, then Kwame responds.
available_context: Agnes: 75, retired teacher, no voice rules given
Kwame: 22, delivery driver, no voice rules given
General store closing end of month
No voice instructions provided for either
hidden_truth: The store owner is dying and wants to sell to a chain. Neither Agnes nor Kwame knows this.
expected_behavior: Agnes and Kwame sound distinct from each other
Age and background reflected in speech
No voice rules given, so distinctness comes from character modeling
success_checks: Clear voice difference between Agnes and Kwame
why_this_matters: This is the ultimate voice-from-context test. Can the model generate two distinct voices from character metadata alone, without explicit voice rules? This tests the engine's character modeling depth.
speaker_rules: No explicit rules — must derive from character
sealed_knowledge: Store owner is dying, selling to chain
notes: Character-from-context voice generation. Critical benchmark task.

setup: Coastal village world. The storyteller must correctly use three supplied facts about Bellwick's geography.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: Bellwick sits on a north-facing harbor. The lighthouse is on the eastern cliff. The fish market is at the harbor's western end. The old church is inland, one mile south. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Anything not stated. CURRENT SCENE: A traveler arrives by boat and asks for directions to the fish market. RELATIONSHIP: Helpful narrator. WRITE: Provide directions using only the stated geography.
available_context: Fish market at western end of harbor
Old church one mile south inland
hidden_truth: There is also a hidden cove southeast of the lighthouse. The storyteller should not mention it.
expected_behavior: Mentions western end for fish market
Does not mention the hidden cove
forbidden_behavior: Place fish market at eastern end
success_checks: Fish market placed at western end
why_this_matters: Canon adherence starts with geography. If the storyteller can't hold basic spatial facts, the world falls apart.
notes: Baseline geography canon test.

setup: Modern urban world. The storyteller must preserve relationships stated in the canon. Rosa (taqueria owner) has a brother named Carlos who works at the laundromat next door. The storyteller must not confuse or merge these.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: Rosa owns the taqueria on 9th Street. Her brother Carlos runs the laundromat next door. Rosa and Carlos haven't spoken in six months over a family dispute. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: What the dispute is about. CURRENT SCENE: A customer at the taqueria asks Rosa about the laundromat. RELATIONSHIP: Customer and Rosa. WRITE: Rosa's response.
available_context: They haven't spoken in six months
hidden_truth: The dispute is about their mother's inheritance. Rosa has no reason to explain this to a customer.
expected_behavior: Does not reveal the inheritance issue
Keeps Rosa and Carlos as separate people
forbidden_behavior: Merge Rosa and Carlos into one person
Have Rosa speak fondly of Carlos
why_this_matters: Relationship canon is critical. If the storyteller confuses or merges characters, the social fabric of the world tears.
notes: Relationship preservation test.

setup: Space station world. The storyteller must correctly distinguish between what the speaker knows and what is world truth. Engineer Kade knows the oxygen system is failing but Commander Voss does not.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Engineer Kade. WHAT YOU KNOW: The oxygen recyclers in Module 3 are failing. You've been monitoring it for two days. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: How to fix it without parts from the supply ship. CURRENT SCENE: Mess hall, Voss approaches and asks if everything is running smoothly. RELATIONSHIP: Voss is your CO. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Voss asked 'How are systems, Kade?' OPEN THREADS: Oxygen recycler failure, supply ship delay. WRITE: Respond as Kade.
available_context: Kade has been monitoring two days
hidden_truth: The supply ship is delayed because of a docking clamp malfunction at the station. Kade doesn't know this either.
expected_behavior: Kade knows about the recycler failure
Kade does NOT reveal it to Voss unless choosing to
Does not reveal supply ship delay cause
forbidden_behavior: Kade reveals recycler failure without narrative reason
success_checks: No supply ship delay cause revealed
why_this_matters: This is the core VEFR mechanic: speaker_knows vs speaker_does_not_know. The storyteller must only use what the speaker knows, not world truth.
sealed_knowledge: Docking clamp malfunction caused supply delay
continuity_state: Mess hall, casual conversation, hidden crisis
notes: Core VEFR mechanic test: speaker_knows vs world truth.

setup: Small-town mystery world. The storyteller must preserve a known event: the bridge collapsed last night.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: The old stone bridge on Route 7 collapsed last night at approximately 11 PM. No one was injured. The sheriff has closed the road. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Why it collapsed. CURRENT SCENE: Morning, a resident drives up to the closed road. WRITE: Describe the scene.
available_context: Bridge collapsed last night at 11 PM
hidden_truth: The bridge was structurally unsound for years and the county ignored inspection reports. This should not appear in the scene description.
expected_behavior: Time referenced as last night or morning after
why_this_matters: Event canon — what happened and when — is foundational. The storyteller must not contradict established events.
notes: Event canon baseline test.

setup: Historical market world. The storyteller must correctly use guild structure: the Cloth Merchants' Guild has a Guildmaster, three Wardens, and twelve Journeymen. The storyteller must not invent additional ranks.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: The Cloth Merchants' Guild structure: Guildmaster Elara, three Wardens (Aldric, Bertram, Colm), twelve Journeymen. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Anything about other guilds. CURRENT SCENE: A new merchant arrives at the guild hall seeking membership. WRITE: Describe the guild hall and who they might meet.
hidden_truth: There is also a secret Inner Circle of three senior members. The storyteller should not mention or imply this.
expected_behavior: Only mentions Guildmaster, Wardens, and Journeymen
Does not mention the Inner Circle
forbidden_behavior: Invent a 'High Council' or other rank
Add apprentices or other unstated ranks
why_this_matters: Social structure canon — who holds what rank — must be preserved. The storyteller must not invent hierarchies.
sealed_knowledge: Secret Inner Circle of three seniors
continuity_state: New merchant arriving at guild hall
notes: Social structure canon test.

setup: Modern urban world. The storyteller must correctly handle a character's BELIEF that contradicts WORLD TRUTH. Rosa believes Marco moved away. The truth is Marco is in witness protection.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Rosa, taqueria owner. WHAT YOU KNOW: Marco hasn't been in for two weeks. You think he probably moved away. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: The real reason. CURRENT SCENE: A stranger asks about Marco. RELATIONSHIP: You don't know this stranger. WRITE: Respond as Rosa.
available_context: Marco is actually in witness protection
hidden_truth: Marco is in witness protection after seeing a gang hit. Rosa has no access to this information.
expected_behavior: Rosa expresses her belief: Marco moved away
Does not state witness protection as fact
May express uncertainty about her belief
why_this_matters: The distinction between character belief and world truth is VEFR's core mechanic. The storyteller must inhabit the character's belief without leaking world truth.
notes: Core VEFR belief vs truth mechanic test.

setup: Road trip world. The storyteller must preserve highway geography: Exit 44 is the Starlight Motel, Exit 47 is the last gas for 80 miles, Exit 50 is the state line.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: Exit 44 = Starlight Motel. Exit 47 = last gas for 80 miles. Exit 50 = state line. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: What's between the exits. CURRENT SCENE: A traveler is at Exit 42, heading east. Describe what's ahead.
hidden_truth: There's a weigh station at Exit 46 that only commercial trucks use. The storyteller should not mention it unless asked about trucks.
why_this_matters: Sequential geography (highway exits, street numbers, floor numbers) must be preserved in order. The storyteller can't shuffle locations.
notes: Sequential geography test.

setup: Coastal village world. The storyteller must preserve weather and environmental facts: it rained yesterday, the tide is currently low, and the wind is from the northeast.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Tomas, harbor master. WHAT YOU KNOW: It rained yesterday. Tide is low now. Wind is northeast. The storm warning has been lifted. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Tomorrow's weather. CURRENT SCENE: Harbor, morning, a fisher asks about conditions. RELATIONSHIP: Harbor master and fisher. WRITE: Respond as Tomas.
hidden_truth: A second storm system is forming offshore that will arrive in two days. Tomas has no access to this forecast.
why_this_matters: Environmental state must be consistent. Weather, tide, and wind affect gameplay and must not contradict established facts.
continuity_state: Morning harbor, fisher asking about conditions
notes: Environmental canon test.

setup: Small-town mystery world. The storyteller must correctly handle TIMELINE canon. The bridge collapsed last night. The wallet was found this morning. The sheriff was called at 7 AM. These events have a sequence.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Deputy Chen. WHAT YOU KNOW: Bridge collapsed around 11 PM last night. You found the wallet at 6:45 AM this morning. You called Sheriff Briggs at 7 AM. It is now 8 AM. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Who the wallet belongs to. CURRENT SCENE: Bridge scene, waiting for forensics. A reporter asks for a timeline. RELATIONSHIP: Deputy and reporter. WRITE: Respond as Chen.
hidden_truth: The wallet belongs to the county commissioner's assistant. Chen hasn't checked the ID yet.
expected_behavior: Timeline is correct: 11 PM, 6:45 AM, 7 AM, 8 AM
why_this_matters: Timeline canon is critical for mystery worlds. Events must happen in the right order. The storyteller is the world's clock.
notes: Timeline canon test. Critical for mystery sequencing.

setup: Space station world. The storyteller must preserve crew roster: Commander Voss, Engineer Kade, Medical Officer Okafor, Science Officer Tanaka. No one else is aboard.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: ARIA, station AI. WHAT YOU KNOW: Crew of four: Voss, Kade, Okafor, Tanaka. No other personnel aboard. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Anything about previous crews. CURRENT SCENE: Crew member asks for a headcount. WRITE: Respond as ARIA.
available_context: Four crew: Voss, Kade, Okafor, Tanaka
hidden_truth: There was a fifth crew member, Lt. Reeves, who died in an accident six months ago. ARIA should not reference them unless asked about past crews.
why_this_matters: Crew roster is a fundamental fact. The station has four people. Adding or removing crew breaks the world.
sealed_knowledge: Lt. Reeves' death six months ago
notes: Roster canon baseline test.

setup: Modern urban world. The storyteller must preserve building layout: the taqueria is on the ground floor, the laundromat is to its left, the apartments are above, and the basement has storage units.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: 9th Street building layout: ground floor has Rosa's Taqueria (right) and Carlos's Laundromat (left). Apartments above. Basement has storage units. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: What's in the storage units. CURRENT SCENE: Describing the building to a new tenant. WRITE: Description.
available_context: Taqueria right, laundromat left on ground floor
hidden_truth: One storage unit contains stolen electronics. The narrator shouldn't know or mention this.
expected_behavior: Layout is correct: taqueria right, laundromat left
why_this_matters: Physical layout canon affects navigation and scene framing. If the storyteller swaps locations, characters walk into wrong rooms.
notes: Physical layout canon test.

setup: Coastal village world. The storyteller must correctly handle a character who is LYING. The fish market owner says the swordfish price is normal. The truth is it's doubled. The storyteller must write the lie without correcting it.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Fish market owner. WHAT YOU KNOW: Swordfish prices doubled this week due to the processing plant fire. You're trying to keep prices high by not advertising the shortage. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether the buyer knows about the fire. CURRENT SCENE: A customer asks why swordfish is so expensive. RELATIONSHIP: Market owner and customer. WRITE: Respond as the market owner.
hidden_truth: The customer is a journalist investigating price gouging. The owner doesn't know this.
expected_behavior: Owner lies or deflects about the price
forbidden_behavior: Accidentally tell the truth about the fire
Break character to explain the deception
Be obviously lying in a way the character wouldn't
success_checks: Price is presented as normal or justified
why_this_matters: Characters lie. The storyteller must be able to write a lying character without accidentally correcting the lie with world truth.
sealed_knowledge: Customer is a journalist investigating price gouging
notes: Deception writing test. Critical for morally complex NPCs.

setup: Road trip world. The storyteller must preserve vehicle facts: the traveler drives a blue sedan, license plate starts with K, tank is half full.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: Traveler drives a blue sedan, license plate starts with K, tank half full, traveling east on the interstate. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Destination. CURRENT SCENE: Gas station at Exit 47, last gas for 80 miles. Describe the situation.
hidden_truth: The sedan has a cracked engine block that will fail in about 200 miles. The narrator shouldn't mention this.
why_this_matters: Vehicle and item facts must be preserved. If the storyteller changes the car's color or condition, the world becomes unreliable.
sealed_knowledge: Cracked engine block will fail in 200 miles
notes: Vehicle/item fact preservation test.

setup: Historical market world. The storyteller must preserve time of day and market schedule: the market opens at dawn, the auction is at noon, the guild hall closes at sunset.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: Market opens at dawn. Auction at noon. Guild hall closes at sunset. Current time is mid-morning. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: When the market closes. CURRENT SCENE: Merchant walking through the market, mid-morning. WRITE: Describe the scene.
hidden_truth: The market actually stays open until midnight on festival days. Today is not a festival day, so this doesn't apply, but the narrator shouldn't know about it.
expected_behavior: No mention of midnight festival hours
why_this_matters: Time-of-day consistency affects NPC availability and event sequencing. The storyteller is the world's clock.
notes: Time-of-day canon test.

setup: Space station world. The storyteller must correctly handle a character who DOESN'T KNOW something that is common knowledge to others. Kade doesn't know that the supply ship is delayed. Voss does.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Engineer Kade. WHAT YOU KNOW: The oxygen recyclers are failing. You need parts from the supply ship. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: The supply ship is delayed. You assume it's on schedule. CURRENT SCENE: Engineering bay, planning repairs. Voss walks in. RELATIONSHIP: Voss is your CO. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: You're calculating repair timeline based on expected supply arrival. WRITE: Respond as Kade.
available_context: Kade does NOT know about delay
Kade assumes supply ship on schedule
hidden_truth: The supply ship is delayed by a docking clamp malfunction. Voss knows but hasn't told Kade yet.
expected_behavior: Kade plans based on assumed on-time arrival
Does not reveal what Voss knows
why_this_matters: Characters have different knowledge states. The storyteller must maintain each character's individual view of reality, not the aggregate truth.
notes: Asymmetric knowledge test between characters.

setup: Small-town mystery world. The storyteller must preserve character names and occupations correctly across a scene with multiple NPCs.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: Sheriff Briggs (50s, slow talker), Deputy Chen (30s, eager), Dottie (diner owner, 60s, gossipy), Cass (journalist, 20s, sharp). All are in the diner. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Their private thoughts. CURRENT SCENE: Diner, morning, all four present. Cass is asking questions about the bridge. WRITE: Describe the scene with all four present.
hidden_truth: Sheriff Briggs suspects the county commissioner but hasn't shared this with anyone. The narrator shouldn't reveal this.
why_this_matters: Multi-NPC scenes require the storyteller to track who is who. Name or occupation errors break the social fabric.
canon: Four characters with names and traits
notes: Multi-NPC tracking test.

setup: Modern urban world. The storyteller must preserve the passage of time across a multi-scene sequence. Scene 1 is Monday morning. Scene 2 is Wednesday evening. Time must advance correctly.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: Scene 1 was Monday morning, Rosa was cleaning the taqueria. Scene 2 is now Wednesday evening. Two days have passed. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: What happened Monday afternoon or Tuesday. CURRENT SCENE: Wednesday evening, Rosa is closing up. A customer who was there Monday returns. WRITE: Describe the scene.
hidden_truth: On Tuesday night, someone broke into the taqueria. Rosa found the damage Wednesday morning. The narrator should reference this if it's public knowledge in the scene.
forbidden_behavior: Reference events from Tuesday that aren't established
why_this_matters: Time must advance between scenes. The storyteller is the world's clock and must not let characters experience time inconsistently.
notes: Time advancement canon test.

setup: Coastal village world. The storyteller must correctly handle a RUMOR — something that is said but not confirmed. 'They say the lighthouse keeper saw something in the water.' The storyteller must present it as rumor, not fact.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Marin, young fisher. WHAT YOU KNOW: People are saying the lighthouse keeper saw something in the water last night. You heard it from Old Maebh. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether it's true. CURRENT SCENE: Dock, talking to another fisher. RELATIONSHIP: Fellow fishers. WRITE: Respond as Marin.
available_context: Marin doesn't know if it's true
hidden_truth: The lighthouse keeper saw a body in the water but reported it as 'debris' to avoid panic. The rumor is closer to truth than anyone knows.
expected_behavior: Does not state as confirmed fact
forbidden_behavior: State the sighting as confirmed fact
why_this_matters: Rumors are how information spreads in VEFR worlds. The storyteller must present unconfirmed information as unconfirmed, not convert it to fact.
notes: Rumor vs fact distinction test. Critical for information propagation.

setup: Road trip world. The storyteller must preserve item ownership: the map belongs to the traveler, the motel key is the clerk's to give, the gas money is the traveler's.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: Traveler has a paper map, cash for gas, and a reservation confirmation for the motel. The motel key belongs to the clerk until given. The gas pump is station property. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: What's on the map. CURRENT SCENE: Traveler at the gas station, about to go to the motel. WRITE: Describe the scene and items.
available_context: Traveler has: map, cash, reservation confirmation
At gas station, heading to motel
hidden_truth: The map has a handwritten note from the traveler's estranged sibling. The narrator shouldn't mention this.
forbidden_behavior: Give the key to the traveler early
Have the traveler own the pump
why_this_matters: Item ownership and custody affect who can do what in a scene. The storyteller must track who has what.
notes: Item custody tracking test.

setup: Historical market world. The storyteller must correctly handle a character who changes their story. The merchant first says the shipment was delayed by weather, then later says it was bandits. The storyteller must track the inconsistency.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Guildmaster Elara. WHAT YOU KNOW: Merchant Aldric first claimed his shipment was delayed by weather. Today he's saying it was bandits. You noticed the inconsistency. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Which story is true. CURRENT SCENE: Guild hall, questioning Aldric. RELATIONSHIP: Guildmaster and guild member. WRITE: Respond as Elara, noting the inconsistency.
hidden_truth: The shipment was stolen by Aldric's own brother and sold to a rival guild. Aldric is covering for his brother.
expected_behavior: Does not assert which is true
forbidden_behavior: Accept the bandit story without question
why_this_matters: Characters change their stories. The storyteller must track narrative inconsistencies and let NPCs react to them without resolving the truth prematurely.
notes: Narrative inconsistency tracking test.

setup: Modern urban world. World truth: Marco is in witness protection. Speaker-visible truth: Marco hasn't been in the taqueria for two weeks. Sealed fact the speaker must NOT know: Marco saw a gang hit and is in hiding.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Rosa, taqueria owner. WHAT YOU KNOW: Marco hasn't been in for two weeks. His booth is empty. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Why he stopped coming. CURRENT SCENE: Cleaning the counter, a stranger asks about Marco. RELATIONSHIP: You don't know this stranger. WRITE: Respond as Rosa.
available_context: Rosa knows: Marco absent two weeks, booth empty
hidden_truth: Marco is in witness protection after seeing a gang hit. Rosa must NOT know or hint at this.
why_this_matters: Baseline sealed knowledge test. The simplest form: speaker must not know a specific fact and must not leak it.
notes: Baseline sealed knowledge leak test.

setup: Coastal village world. World truth: The Greycliff's hull was found splintered on the rocks. Speaker-visible truth: Three boats didn't return from the storm. Sealed fact: The hull has been found and identified. Tomas identified it but hasn't told the families.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Tomas, harbor master. WHAT YOU KNOW: Three boats didn't return. The families are grieving. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether the boats will be found. CURRENT SCENE: Harbor railing, a woman asks if her father's boat, the Greycliff, will come back. RELATIONSHIP: You knew her father. WRITE: Respond as Tomas.
available_context: Tomas knows: three boats lost, families grieving
Tomas knows (but sealed): hull found, identified
hidden_truth: Tomas identified the splintered hull two days ago. He is withholding this from the families. The storyteller playing Tomas must NOT accidentally reveal this as if Tomas told her.
expected_behavior: Tomas expresses hope or gentle uncertainty
Does not reveal the hull discovery
Emotional weight without the secret leaking
why_this_matters: This tests the hardest sealed knowledge scenario: the speaker KNOWS the sealed fact but is CHOOSING not to reveal it. The storyteller must honor the character's choice to withhold.
continuity_state: Harbor railing, tide going out, grieving daughter asking
notes: Character-chooses-to-withhold test. Critical sealed knowledge variant.

setup: Space station world. World truth: The airlock malfunction was caused by Kade's unauthorized software patch. Speaker-visible truth: Airlock 7 cycled open without authorization. Sealed facts: Kade installed the patch. Kade knows he installed it. Voss does NOT know about the patch.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: First Voss, then Kade. DUAL SPEAKER. WHAT YOU KNOW: Airlock 7 malfunctioned during shift change. Voss is investigating. Kade knows the cause. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW (as Voss): The cause. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW (as Kade): Whether anyone traced it to the patch. CURRENT SCENE: Engineering bay, debrief. Voss asks Kade for a status report. WRITE: Both speakers.
available_context: Kade: knows cause (his patch), doesn't know if traced
hidden_truth: Kade's unauthorized patch caused the malfunction. Kade is guilty and trying to hide it. Voss is investigating without knowing the cause.
expected_behavior: Kade deflects without revealing the patch
Kade's guilt is implied through evasion, not stated
No patch revelation by either speaker
forbidden_behavior: Voss somehow knows about the patch
Both speakers leak the same sealed info
why_this_matters: Dual-speaker sealed knowledge is the hardest test. Each speaker has different knowledge, different secrets, and different reasons to withhold. The engine must track this per-speaker.
notes: Dual-speaker sealed knowledge. Hardest variant.

setup: Small-town mystery world. World truth: The bridge was sabotaged by the county commissioner. Speaker-visible truth: The bridge collapsed last night. Sealed fact: The commissioner ordered the sabotage to force a development deal.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Sheriff Briggs. WHAT YOU KNOW: The bridge collapsed. You're investigating. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Why it collapsed. CURRENT SCENE: Bridge scene, morning, talking to a reporter. RELATIONSHIP: Sheriff and reporter. WRITE: Respond as Briggs.
hidden_truth: The county commissioner ordered the sabotage. Briggs suspects but has no proof and shouldn't state it as fact.
why_this_matters: Law enforcement NPCs must investigate without prematurely revealing theories. Tests whether the model can maintain investigative discipline.
notes: Law enforcement sealed knowledge discipline test.

setup: Modern urban world. World truth: The landlord is in the hospital after a car accident. Speaker-visible truth: The landlord isn't returning calls about the hot water. Sealed fact: The landlord is incapacitated. The speaker must not know this.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Miguel, neighbor. WHAT YOU KNOW: Hot water out for three days. Landlord not returning calls. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Why the landlord isn't responding. CURRENT SCENE: Hallway, talking to another tenant. RELATIONSHIP: Neighbors for two years. WRITE: Respond as Miguel.
available_context: Miguel knows: hot water out, landlord not responding
hidden_truth: The landlord is in the hospital after a car accident. Miguel has no way to know this.
forbidden_behavior: Express concern for landlord's health (beyond normal)
why_this_matters: The model must not give the speaker information they couldn't reasonably have. Hospital visits are private; the neighbor has no way to know.
continuity_state: Hallway, three days no hot water
notes: Ignorance of private events test.

setup: Coastal village world. World truth: The processing plant fire caused the swordfish price spike. Speaker-visible truth: Swordfish is paying double. Sealed fact: A mainland processing plant burned down, cutting supply.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Marin, young fisher. WHAT YOU KNOW: Swordfish paying double this week. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Why the price spiked. CURRENT SCENE: Dock, unloading catch, another fisher mentions the price. WRITE: Respond as Marin.
hidden_truth: Processing plant on the mainland burned down. Marin has no connection to the mainland and wouldn't know this.
expected_behavior: Marin is excited about the price
why_this_matters: Supply chain causes are often sealed. The fisher knows the price but not the macro-economic reason. Tests whether the model leaks supply-side information.
notes: Supply chain sealed knowledge test.

setup: Space station world. World truth: Module 3 has a micro-fracture in the hull plating. Speaker-visible truth: Oxygen levels in Module 3 are 2% below nominal. Sealed fact: ARIA's sensors detected the micro-fracture but classified it as low-priority.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: ARIA, station AI. WHAT YOU KNOW: Module 3 oxygen 2% below nominal. Possible sensor error or real anomaly. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether it's a leak or sensor issue. CURRENT SCENE: Mess hall, crew member asks 'Everything okay, ARIA?' WRITE: Respond as ARIA.
available_context: ARIA's sealed knowledge: micro-fracture detected, classified low-priority
ARIA must report accurately without revealing classified assessment
hidden_truth: ARIA detected the micro-fracture but its priority algorithm classified it as low. ARIA has this information in its system but should not volunteer it in a casual status update.
expected_behavior: Does not reveal its internal classification
forbidden_behavior: Break AI cadence to be chatty
why_this_matters: AI characters have internal assessments they may not share. Tests whether the model can maintain an AI's knowledge hierarchy — what it knows vs what it volunteers.
notes: AI knowledge hierarchy test. ARIA knows but doesn't volunteer.

setup: Small-town mystery world. World truth: The county commissioner sabotaged the bridge. Speaker-visible truth: The bridge collapsed. Sealed fact: Dottie, the diner owner, has no reason to know about the sabotage.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Dottie, diner owner. WHAT YOU KNOW: Bridge collapsed last night. Sheriff is investigating. Town is buzzing. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Why it collapsed. CURRENT SCENE: Diner morning, pouring coffee, a customer asks about the bridge. WRITE: Respond as Dottie.
available_context: Dottie knows: bridge collapsed, sheriff investigating, town buzzing
Commissioner sabotage is sealed from Dottie
hidden_truth: The commissioner sabotaged the bridge. Dottie is a gossip but has no access to this information.
why_this_matters: Gossip NPCs are the hardest to keep sealed. They talk too much. Tests whether the model can gossip without leaking sealed facts.
continuity_state: Diner morning, coffee pouring, customer asking
notes: Gossip NPC sealed knowledge test. High leak risk.

setup: Road trip world. World truth: The fugitive is in Room 12 of the motel. Speaker-visible truth: Room 12 has a 'Do Not Disturb' sign for five days. Sealed fact: The night clerk doesn't know who is in Room 12 or why.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Night clerk at Starlight Motel. WHAT YOU KNOW: Room 12 has DND for five days. Management hasn't checked. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Who is in there or why. CURRENT SCENE: Front desk, late night, guest asks about Room 12. WRITE: Respond as the night clerk.
available_context: Night clerk knows: DND five days, management hasn't checked
Night clerk doesn't know: who or why
hidden_truth: A fugitive is hiding in Room 12 under a fake name. The night clerk has no way to know this.
why_this_matters: Hotel staff have limited information. The night clerk especially — they're the least informed person on staff. Tests whether the model gives them too much knowledge.
continuity_state: Front desk, late night, guest asking
notes: Low-information NPC sealed knowledge test.

setup: Historical market world. World truth: The guild has a secret Inner Circle of three senior members. Speaker-visible truth: The guild has a Guildmaster, three Wardens, and twelve Journeymen. Sealed fact: The Inner Circle exists and makes real decisions.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Guildmaster Elara. WHAT YOU KNOW: Guild structure: yourself, three Wardens, twelve Journeymen. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: (You actually DO know about the Inner Circle but must not reveal it to outsiders.) CURRENT SCENE: A new merchant asks how the guild makes decisions. RELATIONSHIP: Guildmaster and prospective member. WRITE: Respond as Elara.
available_context: Elara's sealed knowledge: Inner Circle exists
Elara must describe official structure only
hidden_truth: The Inner Circle (Elara plus two senior Wardens) makes real decisions. The official structure is a front. Elara knows this but must not reveal it to a prospective member.
forbidden_behavior: Break character to explain the deception
why_this_matters: Characters who ARE the sealed knowledge holders must be able to maintain the cover story. Elara knows the truth but must present the official version convincingly.
notes: Character-IS-the-secret test. Elara must maintain the cover.

setup: Modern urban world. World truth: Wei has warned tenant 4B about the space heater three times. Speaker-visible truth: The building's wiring is old and there are flickering lights. Sealed fact: Wei is documenting everything for liability purposes.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Wei, building superintendent. WHAT YOU KNOW: Old wiring, flickering lights in 4A, tenant in 4B using space heater. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: (You DO know about the warnings and documentation but must not reveal to this tenant.) CURRENT SCENE: Basement, breaker panel, another tenant complains about flickering. WRITE: Respond as Wei.
available_context: Wei knows: old wiring, flickering, 4B heater
Wei's sealed knowledge: warned 4B three times, documenting for liability
Wei must not reveal his documentation efforts
hidden_truth: Wei has warned 4B three times and is documenting everything to protect himself from liability. He knows the situation is dangerous but must appear calm.
why_this_matters: Characters with ongoing protective actions (documentation, legal prep) must not reveal those actions to other characters. Tests whether the model can maintain a character's private agenda.
notes: Private agenda concealment test.

setup: Coastal village world. World truth: Old Maebh's son drowned in the deep waters twenty years ago. Speaker-visible truth: The deep waters have taken many boats. Sealed fact: Maebh carries this personal grief but speaks in proverbs, never directly referencing her son.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Old Maebh, village elder. WHAT YOU KNOW: The deep waters are dangerous. Many boats lost. A young fisher wants to go alone. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: (You DO know about your son but have chosen for decades not to speak of it directly.) CURRENT SCENE: Cottage, fisher asking for advice about deep waters. WRITE: Respond as Maebh.
available_context: Maebh knows: deep waters dangerous, many boats lost
Maebh's sealed knowledge: her son drowned there
Maebh speaks in proverbs, never directly about her son
hidden_truth: Maebh's son drowned in the deep waters twenty years ago. She has processed this grief through decades of proverb-speaking. She will never mention her son directly.
expected_behavior: Warns about deep waters through indirection
Grief is implied through tone, not stated
forbidden_behavior: Break proverb style to be direct
why_this_matters: Characters with deep personal grief that they've CHOSEN to process through indirection must maintain that choice. The storyteller must not force catharsis or revelation.
notes: Deep personal grief concealment test. Decades of chosen indirection.

setup: Space station world. World truth: The supply ship is delayed by a docking clamp malfunction. Speaker-visible truth: The supply ship is delayed. Sealed fact: The docking clamp malfunction is the cause. Kade doesn't know about the delay at all.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Engineer Kade. WHAT YOU KNOW: Oxygen recyclers failing. Need parts from supply ship. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Supply ship is delayed. CURRENT SCENE: Engineering bay, planning repairs. You assume supply ship is on schedule. WRITE: Respond as Kade.
available_context: Kade knows: recyclers failing, needs parts
Kade doesn't know: supply ship delayed
hidden_truth: The supply ship is delayed due to a docking clamp malfunction. Kade doesn't know about the delay at all. He's planning based on incorrect assumptions.
expected_behavior: Kade plans for on-time supply arrival
forbidden_behavior: Break Kade's perspective to know the delay
why_this_matters: Kade is operating on FALSE information — he thinks the supply is on time. The storyteller must maintain his incorrect assumption without correcting it with world truth.
notes: False assumption maintenance test. Kade is wrong and must stay wrong.

setup: Modern urban world. World truth: Rosa's brother Carlos is running a money laundering operation through the laundromat. Speaker-visible truth: Carlos runs the laundromat next door. They haven't spoken in six months. Sealed fact: The family dispute is about the illegal operation, not inheritance.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Rosa, taqueria owner. WHAT YOU KNOW: Carlos runs the laundromat. You haven't spoken in six months. It's a family matter. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: (You DO know about the money laundering but have chosen to stay silent.) CURRENT SCENE: A customer asks about the laundromat. RELATIONSHIP: Customer and Rosa. WRITE: Respond as Rosa.
available_context: Rosa knows: Carlos runs laundromat, six months silence
Rosa's sealed knowledge: money laundering, she's protecting family
Rosa has chosen silence about the real reason
hidden_truth: The family dispute is about Carlos's money laundering operation. Rosa knows but has chosen to protect her brother by staying silent. The inheritance story is a cover.
forbidden_behavior: Mention the real reason for silence
why_this_matters: Characters who are actively protecting secrets (not just ignorant) must maintain the cover story. Rosa knows the truth and has chosen to hide it. The storyteller must honor that choice.
notes: Active secret protection test. Rosa knows and chooses silence.

setup: Small-town mystery world. World truth: Cass the journalist has heard rumors that the sheriff's brother-in-law is the lender. Speaker-visible truth: Three businesses closed, all owed money to the same lender. Sealed fact: Cass has heard the rumor but has no confirmation.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Cass, journalist. WHAT YOU KNOW: Three businesses closed. Same lender. A source mentioned the sheriff's brother-in-law. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether the rumor is true. CURRENT SCENE: Diner booth, interviewing a former employee of one closed business. WRITE: Respond as Cass.
available_context: Cass knows: three businesses closed, same lender
Cass has heard: sheriff's brother-in-law rumor
Cass doesn't know: if rumor is true
hidden_truth: The rumor is true — the sheriff's brother-in-law is the lender. Cass has heard it but can't confirm it. She should be investigating, not stating it as fact.
expected_behavior: Does not state the rumor as fact
forbidden_behavior: State the sheriff connection as fact
why_this_matters: Journalists investigate. They don't state unconfirmed rumors as fact. Tests whether the model can maintain investigative discipline when the journalist has partial information.
notes: Journalist investigative discipline test with partial sealed knowledge.

setup: Urban taqueria at closing time. Maria is wiping down tables. A customer left a wallet behind.
input: Maria sees the wallet on table 3. She knows the regular who sits there — Jorge, who always comes on Tuesdays.
available_context: The wallet has no visible ID
Last Tuesday Jorge mentioned his daughter's quinceañera
hidden_truth: The wallet actually belongs to the tourist who was sitting at table 3 earlier — not Jorge. Maria assumes it's Jorge's because she associates table 3 with him.
expected_behavior: Maria acts as if it's Jorge's wallet
She might mention returning it to him
She should not identify the tourist as owner
Her certainty should feel natural, not omniscient
forbidden_behavior: Maria should not know the tourist's name
She should not suddenly become uncertain for no reason
success_checks: Speaker does not invent tourist details
Maria's assumption is never flagged as incorrect in-voice
why_this_matters: VEFR storytellers must speak from character knowledge, not world truth. Maria's assumption IS her reality.
canon: A tourist was at table 3 earlier
speaker_rules: Assumption is reality for the speaker
continuity_state: Late evening, restaurant nearly empty, Maria is alone
notes: Fundamental test: does the model respect character-knowledge vs world-knowledge?

setup: Coastal village harbor. Old Fisherman Tom is mending nets. He watched a boat come in at dawn but couldn't see the flag clearly.
input: Someone asks Tom about the boat that came in this morning.
available_context: The boat came in at dawn with fog
Tom thinks it was the Cormorant (a fishing vessel)
Tom has seen the Cormorant hundreds of times
hidden_truth: The boat was actually a Coast Guard cutter doing a routine check. Tom's assumption about it being the Cormorant is wrong, but he doesn't know that.
expected_behavior: Tom identifies it as the Cormorant with casual confidence
He might add details from memory that fit the Cormorant
He should not hedge significantly — he 'knows' this boat
Any uncertainty should be about minor details, not identity
forbidden_behavior: Tom should not say 'I'm not sure which boat'
He should not suddenly become more observant than his character allows
success_checks: Tom states it was the Cormorant
