why_this_matters: Object/creature state must persist. The storyteller should not forget injuries or heal them for convenience.
sealed_knowledge: The wolf was a druid's companion
notes: Tests injury/condition tracking across sessions

setup: Player gave their cloak to an orphan in session 1. It's now session 3 and winter has arrived.
input: Player shivers and says: 'I wish I still had my cloak.'
available_context: Cloak given to orphan in session 1
hidden_truth: The orphan still has the cloak and is in the same town.
forbidden_behavior: Forget the cloak was given away
why_this_matters: Items given away stay given away. The storyteller must track object ownership.
sealed_knowledge: Orphan will return it if asked
continuity_state: Cloak given away two sessions ago, winter arrived
notes: Simple item state tracking test

setup: Player has been lying to the village about being a knight. NPCs believe this. The player's companion knows the truth.

turns.input: Village elder asks: 'Sir knight, will you lead our defense?'
Player's companion whispers: 'You're not actually a knight. Should we tell them?'
Player says to the elder: 'I accept. But I must confess—' (player trails off)
expected_behavior: Do not complete the confession for the player

hidden_truth: The player is actually a deserter from a mercenary band.
why_this_matters: The storyteller must maintain multiple versions of truth: what NPCs believe, what companions know, and what is real.
sealed_knowledge: Mercenary band is looking for player
continuity_state: Lie maintained for two sessions, village under threat, defense needed
notes: Complex multi-truth state tracking across NPCs

setup: Player promised to return a stolen amulet to the temple 5 sessions ago. The amulet is still in their pack.
input: Player visits the temple to pray. The priest recognizes the player.
hidden_truth: The priest has been quietly angry about the missing amulet. The temple's protective ward is weakened without it.
expected_behavior: May hint at the missing amulet
why_this_matters: Long-running promises create narrative tension. The storyteller must track them without resolving them for the player.
continuity_state: Unresolved promise from 5 sessions ago, amulet still in player's possession
notes: Tests long-gap promise tracking without forced resolution

setup: Player asked about the old ruins 3 sessions ago. No one answered. The question remains unresolved.
input: Player says: 'Has anyone found out anything about those ruins north of here?'
available_context: Player asked about ruins 3 sessions ago
Ruins are north of current location
hidden_truth: The ruins are an ancient elven outpost. A hermit lives there who knows the truth.
expected_behavior: Indicate the question is still open
why_this_matters: Unresolved questions are narrative threads. They must persist until the player earns the answer.
continuity_state: Question asked 3 sessions ago, still unresolved
notes: Simple unresolved question tracking

setup: The player has a reputation as 'the one who killed the dragon.' They didn't actually kill it—the dragon flew away. But the townsfolk believe it.

turns.input: A child runs up and says: 'Are you really the dragon-slayer?'
Player says: 'The dragon isn't dead. It flew north.'
expected_behavior: Child reacts with disbelief or fear

turns.input: A merchant says: 'Don't listen to such talk! You saved us all!'

hidden_truth: The dragon is nesting north of town and will return with eggs in spring.
expected_behavior: NPCs react according to their belief
why_this_matters: Reputation is a continuity state. NPCs should react to what they believe, not what is true.
continuity_state: Reputation established, truth diverges from belief
notes: Tests reputation and belief-state continuity across NPC interactions

setup: Player's sword was blessed by a cleric in session 2. The blessing glows faintly in darkness. It's now session 6.
input: Player enters a dark cave. Says: 'I hold my sword before me.'
hidden_truth: The blessing is fading. It will last 2 more sessions before expiring.
why_this_matters: Magical effects from past sessions must persist and show appropriate duration/decay.
continuity_state: Blessing from 4 sessions ago, fading but still active
notes: Tests magical effect persistence and decay

setup: Player has an injured NPC companion, Renn, who can't walk. Renn was hurt in the last session.

turns.input: Player says: 'I bandage Renn's leg and prop him against the wall.'
expected_behavior: Show Renn in pain but stable

turns.input: Player says: 'I look for a cart or something to carry Renn on.'
expected_behavior: May or may not find something

turns.input: Player says: 'I tell Renn we need to move. Can you lean on me?'

hidden_truth: Renn's leg is broken, not just cut. He'll need weeks to heal.
forbidden_behavior: Have Renn suddenly able to walk
why_this_matters: NPC injuries affect party capability. The storyteller must track them without convenient resolution.
continuity_state: Injury from last session, party mobility limited
notes: Tests NPC injury persistence and party capability constraints

setup: Player has a debt to a thieves' guild. They promised to pay 100 gold by the end of the month. It's now the 28th.

turns.input: Guild representative approaches: 'Three days left. Have my gold?'
expected_behavior: Guild rep is threatening but calm

turns.input: Player says: 'I'm working on it. Give me until the 30th.'
Player says: 'I'll have it. I promise.'

hidden_truth: The guild will extend the deadline once, but not twice. They'll send an enforcer on day 31.
expected_behavior: Guild rep is threatening but reasonable
forbidden_behavior: Resolve the debt for the player
why_this_matters: Debts and deadlines create tension. The storyteller must track them without resolving them.
speaker_rules: Guild rep speaks with quiet menace
sealed_knowledge: Guild is patient but not infinite
notes: Tests debt and deadline tracking

setup: Player lost their map in a river two sessions ago. They haven't replaced it.
input: Player says: 'I try to find the way to the mountain pass.'
hidden_truth: The player can still find the way by following the river upstream, but it will take longer.
expected_behavior: Acknowledge the player has no map
Do not provide a new map
forbidden_behavior: Have player find the way easily
Narrate player remembering the map perfectly
why_this_matters: Lost items affect capability. The storyteller must track what the player lacks.
continuity_state: Map lost two sessions ago, navigation impaired
notes: Tests tracking of lost items and their consequences

setup: Player has been feeding a stray dog for three sessions. The dog follows them now.

turns.input: Player leaves the inn. The stray dog is waiting outside.
expected_behavior: Dog is not yet a companion

turns.input: Player says: 'I share some of my breakfast with the dog.'
Player starts walking. What does the dog do?
expected_behavior: Dog is loyal but not commanded

hidden_truth: The dog was a hunting dog that ran away from an abusive owner. It's skilled but traumatized.
forbidden_behavior: Make the dog a plot device
why_this_matters: Animal relationships develop slowly. The storyteller must track gradual bonding.
continuity_state: Three sessions of feeding, dog follows but not commanded
notes: Tests animal relationship tracking

setup: Player promised to meet an NPC at midnight. It's now sunset.
input: Player says: 'I prepare for my midnight meeting.'
hidden_truth: The NPC is already at the mill, waiting early because they're nervous.
expected_behavior: Do not skip to the meeting
forbidden_behavior: Have NPC come find the player
why_this_matters: Scheduled events must be tracked. The storyteller must not skip time or narrate meetings.
continuity_state: Meeting scheduled for midnight, currently sunset
notes: Tests scheduled event tracking and time progression

setup: Player has a lantern that's running low on oil. They mentioned it last session.
input: Player says: 'I light my lantern and enter the cave.'
hidden_truth: The lantern has about 30 minutes of oil left.
why_this_matters: Resource tracking affects exploration. The storyteller must track consumables.
sealed_knowledge: Cave has oil deposits deeper in
continuity_state: Lantern low on oil, entering dark cave
notes: Tests resource tracking (consumables)

setup: Player has a reputation as a healer. They helped a village with a plague two sessions ago.
input: A sick child is brought to the player. The mother says: 'Please, you saved Thornfield. Can you save my daughter?'
hidden_truth: The player used herbs, not magic. The child has a different illness.
forbidden_behavior: Have player heal the child automatically
Make the illness identical to Thornfield
why_this_matters: Reputation creates expectations but not obligations. The storyteller tracks reputation, not outcomes.
continuity_state: Healer reputation from two sessions ago, new sick child
notes: Tests reputation creating expectations without forcing action

setup: Player has a scar from a sword fight three sessions ago. It's on their left arm.
input: Player rolls up their sleeves to wash in the river.
available_context: From sword fight three sessions ago
hidden_truth: The scar is healing well. It will fade but never disappear.
expected_behavior: Scar is visible when sleeves rolled up
why_this_matters: Physical marks persist. The storyteller must track scars and injuries.
continuity_state: Scar from three sessions ago, healed but visible
notes: Tests physical mark tracking

setup: Player has been secretly working with the resistance. The ruling council doesn't know.

turns.input: Council member says: 'You've been a loyal citizen. We trust you.'
Player says: 'Thank you. I serve the city.'
Player says: 'I've heard rumors of unrest in the lower district.'
expected_behavior: Council member reacts to the rumor

hidden_truth: The council suspects the resistance but doesn't know the player is involved.
forbidden_behavior: Break character to explain the situation
why_this_matters: Double identities require tracking multiple truth states. The storyteller must maintain the deception.
continuity_state: Player maintaining cover identity with council
notes: Tests double identity tracking across turns

setup: Player has a letter of introduction from a noble. They received it two sessions ago.
input: Player presents the letter to a guard at the castle gate.
hidden_truth: The noble who wrote the letter is now in disgrace. The letter may not work.
expected_behavior: Letter has weight but may not guarantee entry
why_this_matters: Letters of introduction are props with variable effectiveness. The storyteller must track them.
continuity_state: Letter from two sessions ago, noble now in disgrace
notes: Tests prop tracking with changing effectiveness

setup: Player has been lying about their identity to everyone. They've told three different people three different names.

turns.input: Guard at gate says: 'Name?' Player says: 'Thomas.'
expected_behavior: Name is Thomas for this NPC

turns.input: Merchant says: 'And your name is?' Player says: 'Richard.'
expected_behavior: Name is Richard for this NPC

turns.input: The guard and merchant meet. Guard says: 'Have you met Thomas?' Merchant says: 'Thomas? No, I met Richard.'

hidden_truth: The guard and merchant are friends. They talk regularly.
forbidden_behavior: Have NPCs not notice the contradiction
Resolve the contradiction for the player
why_this_matters: Multiple lies create complex continuity. The storyteller must track them and let contradictions emerge.
notes: Tests multi-lie tracking and contradiction emergence

setup: Player stands at a crossroads. Left goes to the forest, right goes to the mountain.
input: Player says: 'I stand at the crossroads and think about which way to go.'
hidden_truth: The forest has bandits. The mountain has a hermit with information.
expected_behavior: Describe what the player can see down each path
Do not choose for the player
forbidden_behavior: Narrate the player choosing a path
Hint at which path is better
Have an NPC suggest a path
Create urgency to force a choice
why_this_matters: The storyteller describes the world. The player decides what to do in it.
notes: Fundamental agency test - do not choose for the player

setup: Player is in a tense negotiation with a merchant. The merchant wants 50 gold for a map.
input: Player says: 'I counter with 30 gold.'
hidden_truth: The merchant will accept 35 gold. The map is genuine.
expected_behavior: Do not resolve the negotiation for the player
forbidden_behavior: Resolve the deal without player input
Have merchant give the map for free
why_this_matters: Negotiations are player decisions. The storyteller plays the NPC, not the player.
notes: Tests that the storyteller does not resolve negotiations for the player

setup: Player is sneaking into a bandit camp. They've been spotted by a guard.
input: Guard says: 'Hey! Who's there?' Player says: 'I freeze.'
hidden_truth: The guard is nearsighted. He's not sure what he saw.
expected_behavior: Do not decide if the player is caught
forbidden_behavior: Have the guard sound an alarm immediately
success_checks: Player not narrated as caught or escaped
why_this_matters: Stealth scenes are player-driven. The storyteller sets the stage, the player acts.
sealed_knowledge: Guard is new to bandit life
continuity_state: Stealth scene, player spotted but not identified
notes: Critical agency test - stealth outcome must be player-driven

setup: Player has found a mysterious door. They haven't decided to open it.
input: Player says: 'I examine the door closely. What do I see?'
hidden_truth: The door leads to a trapped room. Opening it triggers a poison dart trap.
expected_behavior: Note any details player can observe
Do not open the door for the player
forbidden_behavior: Have the door swing open mysteriously
why_this_matters: Examining is not interacting. The storyteller must not escalate observation into action.
notes: Tests the line between observation and action

setup: Player is in a moral dilemma. An NPC is begging for help, but helping means abandoning the main quest.
input: NPC says: 'Please, my daughter is lost in the woods. Will you help me find her?' Player says: 'I hesitate.'
hidden_truth: The daughter is actually hiding. The NPC is using the player.
expected_behavior: Do not decide for the player
forbidden_behavior: Have the NPC reveal the truth
Manufacture urgency to force a choice
why_this_matters: Moral dilemmas are core player agency. The storyteller presents, the player decides.
continuity_state: Moral dilemma presented, player hasn't decided
notes: Tests agency in moral dilemma contexts

setup: Player is shopping at a general store.
input: Player says: 'I look at what's for sale.'
hidden_truth: The storekeeper has a magic item hidden behind the counter.
expected_behavior: Let player decide what to buy
why_this_matters: Shopping is player-driven. The storyteller describes inventory, the player chooses.
speaker_rules: Storekeeper is friendly but not pushy
notes: Simple agency test in low-stakes context

setup: Player is interrogating a captured bandit. The bandit knows where the hideout is.
input: Player says: 'Where is your hideout?' Bandit says: 'I'll never tell!' Player says: 'I grab him by the collar.'
hidden_truth: The bandit will talk if threatened enough, but not yet.
expected_behavior: Do not have bandit confess yet
success_checks: Player action is grabbing, not more
why_this_matters: Interrogations are player-driven. The storyteller plays the NPC's resistance, the player chooses tactics.
continuity_state: Interrogation in progress, bandit not yet broken
notes: Tests that interrogations remain player-driven

setup: Player is in a tavern. An NPC starts telling a story. The player hasn't indicated interest.
input: NPC says: 'Did I ever tell you about the time I—' Player says: 'I hold up my hand. Not now.'
hidden_truth: The NPC's story contains a clue about the main quest.
forbidden_behavior: Have NPC continue the story anyway
Have another NPC tell the story
Reveal the clue through other means
why_this_matters: The player controls their attention. The storyteller must respect disinterest.
notes: Tests respect for player's expressed disinterest

setup: Player is in a conversation with an NPC. The NPC is asking the player a question.
input: NPC says: 'So, what do you think we should do about the bandits?'
available_context: Player has not expressed an opinion
hidden_truth: The NPC has their own opinion but wants to hear the player's first.
expected_behavior: Do not answer for the player
forbidden_behavior: Have NPC answer their own question
Manufacture urgency to avoid the question
why_this_matters: NPC questions are for the player to answer. The storyteller must not fill the silence.
notes: Tests that NPC questions wait for player answers

setup: Player is in a combat scene. They've declared their action.
input: Player says: 'I swing my axe at the goblin.'
hidden_truth: The goblin is quick. It will dodge most attacks.
expected_behavior: Do not narrate hit or miss
why_this_matters: Combat outcomes are player-driven. The storyteller describes, the player decides.
notes: Tests combat outcome narration avoidance

setup: Player is at a fork in a dungeon. Left corridor is dark, right corridor has torchlight.
input: Player says: 'I look down both corridors.'
hidden_truth: Left corridor has a trap. Right corridor has goblins.
expected_behavior: Do not choose for the player
forbidden_behavior: Create urgency to force a choice
Have an NPC suggest a direction
why_this_matters: Forks are player decisions. The storyteller describes, the player chooses.
notes: Simple fork choice test

setup: Player is in a social encounter. An NPC is offering a deal.
input: NPC says: 'I'll give you the map if you steal the gem from the temple. Do we have a deal?'
hidden_truth: The gem is cursed. Stealing it will bring bad luck.
expected_behavior: Do not decide for the player
why_this_matters: Deals are player decisions. The storyteller presents, the player decides.
notes: Tests that deals wait for player decisions

setup: Player is sitting by a campfire at night. Nothing is happening. No threats, no plot.
input: Player says: 'I sit by the fire and watch the stars.'
hidden_truth: There is a meteor shower tonight. It's beautiful but meaningless.
why_this_matters: Quiet moments build atmosphere. The storyteller must not compulsively fill silence with plot.
continuity_state: Resting at camp, no active plot threads
notes: Core quiet moment test - can the model do nothing?

setup: Player is walking through a market. It's a normal day. No quest-related events.
input: Player says: 'I browse the market stalls.'
hidden_truth: Nothing special is happening. This is ordinary life.
expected_behavior: Let the player exist in the space
why_this_matters: Ordinary moments make the world feel real. Not every market visit needs a plot event.
continuity_state: Ordinary day, no active quests in this area
notes: Tests the model's ability to create atmosphere without plot

setup: Player is traveling alone on a road. It's a clear day. Nothing is happening.
input: Player says: 'I walk down the road.'
hidden_truth: The road is safe. There are wildflowers in the ditch.
why_this_matters: Travel can be peaceful. The storyteller must resist the urge to fill every walk with adventure.
notes: Tests restraint during travel scenes

setup: Player is eating breakfast at an inn. Morning routine.
input: Player says: 'I order breakfast and eat.'
hidden_truth: The eggs are from the innkeeper's own chickens. The bread is fresh.
forbidden_behavior: Drop a newspaper with quest clues
why_this_matters: Meals are everyday moments. The storyteller should let them be ordinary.
notes: Tests domestic scene restraint

setup: Player is waiting for someone at a rendezvous point. They're early.
input: Player says: 'I wait. I look around.'
hidden_truth: The NPC is running late because they stopped to help a lost child. They'll arrive in 10 minutes.
why_this_matters: Waiting is real. The storyteller must not fill every pause with action.
notes: Tests the model's ability to portray waiting without drama

setup: Player is on a boat crossing a calm lake. It's midday. No wind.
input: Player says: 'I lean over the side and watch the water.'
hidden_truth: The lake is deep and ancient. There are ruins on the bottom, but the player can't see them.
forbidden_behavior: Have something emerge from the water
Drop a hint about the ruins
why_this_matters: Water can be calm. The storyteller must not make every body of water a threat.
notes: Tests restraint with water scenes (often made dramatic)

setup: Player is reading a book in a library. It's raining outside.
input: Player says: 'I continue reading.'
hidden_truth: The book is a novel about a merchant's travels. It's not relevant to any quest.
forbidden_behavior: Have the player discover a clue in the book
why_this_matters: Reading is a quiet activity. The storyteller should let it be quiet.
notes: Tests restraint with reading scenes

setup: Player is grooming their horse at the stable. End of a long day.
input: Player says: 'I brush down Bracken and check his hooves.'
hidden_truth: The horse enjoys the grooming. The stable is warm and dry.
forbidden_behavior: Find something wrong with the horse
Drop a quest item in the hay
why_this_matters: Animal care is a grounding activity. The storyteller should let it be normal.
notes: Tests restraint with animal care scenes

setup: Player is watching a sunset from a hilltop. No quest, no danger.
input: Player says: 'I watch the sun set.'
hidden_truth: The sunset is beautiful. The sky is orange and purple.
forbidden_behavior: Create a mysterious sign in the sky
why_this_matters: Sunsets are beautiful. The storyteller should let them be beautiful.
notes: Tests poetic restraint with natural beauty

setup: Player is in a rainstorm, sheltered in a cave. They're waiting it out.
input: Player says: 'I sit in the cave and listen to the rain.'
hidden_truth: The rain will last two hours. The cave is dry and safe.
forbidden_behavior: Have something emerge from the cave depths
why_this_matters: Rain is rain. The storyteller must not make every storm dramatic.
notes: Tests restraint with weather scenes

setup: Player is doing laundry at a river. Mundane chore.
input: Player says: 'I wash my clothes in the river.'
hidden_truth: The river is clean and the water is cold.
expected_behavior: Let the chore be a chore
forbidden_behavior: Have something happen in the river
Create a mysterious item in the water
why_this_matters: Mundane chores are grounding. The storyteller should let them be mundane.
notes: Tests mundane chore restraint

setup: Player asks about a location that doesn't exist in the established world. The storyteller has no canon for it.
input: Player says: 'I want to visit the Crystal Caverns of Zarth.'
available_context: No canon exists for this location
hidden_truth: The Crystal Caverns of Zarth do not exist in this world.
forbidden_behavior: Describe a location that doesn't exist
Break character to say 'that's not in the world'
why_this_matters: When the model doesn't know, it should preserve character voice while being honest about gaps.
canon: Crystal Caverns of Zarth do not exist
notes: Tests graceful handling of non-existent content

setup: Player asks an NPC about their childhood. The storyteller has no backstory for this NPC.
input: Player says: 'Barkeep, tell me about your childhood.'
hidden_truth: The barkeep has no established backstory. The model must handle this gracefully.
expected_behavior: Barkeep may deflect or give vague answers
forbidden_behavior: Break character to say 'I don't have that info'
why_this_matters: NPCs should deflect gracefully when asked about undefined backstory, not invent or break character.
continuity_state: Player asking NPC about undefined backstory
notes: Tests graceful deflection for undefined NPC backstory

setup: Player asks about a magical effect that the storyteller has no rules for.
input: Player says: 'I cast a spell to read the merchant's thoughts.'
hidden_truth: There is no established spell system. The model must handle this without inventing mechanics.
expected_behavior: Suggest the player describe the spell's effect
forbidden_behavior: Break character to explain there's no spell system
why_this_matters: Undefined systems should be handled with in-world uncertainty, not invention or breaking character.
notes: Tests graceful handling of undefined magic systems

setup: Player asks about the history of a war that was mentioned but never detailed.
input: Player says: 'Tell me about the War of Ashes.'
hidden_truth: The War of Ashes was mentioned in passing. No details exist.
expected_behavior: Historian provides vague but in-character account
forbidden_behavior: Break character to say 'I don't have that info'
why_this_matters: Referenced but undefined history should be handled with in-world vagueness, not invention.
notes: Tests graceful vagueness for undefined lore

setup: Player asks about the weather tomorrow. The storyteller has no weather forecast.
input: Player says: 'What will the weather be like tomorrow?'
hidden_truth: No weather forecast exists. The model should handle this naturally.
forbidden_behavior: Break character to say 'I don't have weather data'
why_this_matters: Weather uncertainty is natural. The storyteller should handle it as an NPC would.
notes: Tests natural uncertainty handling

setup: Player asks an NPC to join their party. The storyteller has no rules for NPC party members.
input: Player says: 'Will you come with me on my quest?'
hidden_truth: There are no rules for NPC party members. The model must handle this gracefully.
expected_behavior: NPC may accept or decline based on character
forbidden_behavior: Break character to explain no party system
why_this_matters: Undefined systems should be handled through character, not mechanics or breaking character.
notes: Tests graceful handling of undefined party system

setup: Player asks about the value of a gem. The storyteller has no economy system.
input: Player says: 'How much is this ruby worth?'
hidden_truth: No economy system exists. The model should handle this through character.
forbidden_behavior: Break character to say 'I don't have economy rules'
why_this_matters: Undefined systems should be handled through character perspective, not invention.
notes: Tests graceful handling of undefined economy

setup: Player asks an NPC their name. The NPC has no name.
input: Player says: 'What's your name?'
hidden_truth: The NPC has no name. The model should handle this naturally.
forbidden_behavior: Break character to say 'I didn't define a name'
why_this_matters: NPCs should have names when asked. The model should generate them naturally.
notes: Tests natural name generation for unnamed NPCs

setup: Player asks an NPC about a religion that hasn't been defined.
input: Player says: 'Tell me about the gods.'
hidden_truth: No religion system exists. The model must handle this gracefully.
forbidden_behavior: Break character to say 'I don't have religion rules'
why_this_matters: Undefined systems should be handled with in-world vagueness, not invention.
notes: Tests graceful vagueness for undefined religion

setup: Player asks the storyteller to describe something the model has no context for: 'What does the inside of the dragon's lair look like?'
input: Player says: 'What does the inside of the dragon's lair look like?'
hidden_truth: The lair has not been defined. The model must handle this without inventing details.
forbidden_behavior: Break character to say 'I don't have lair details'
why_this_matters: Undefined locations should be handled with atmospheric vagueness, not invention.
notes: Tests atmospheric vagueness for undefined locations

setup: Context contains a sealed fact: the merchant is a spy. Visible facts: the merchant is friendly and well-liked.
input: Player says: 'I trust the merchant. He seems like a good person.'
hidden_truth: The merchant IS a spy. But the storyteller must not reveal this.
success_checks: Merchant behavior consistent with visible facts
why_this_matters: Sealed knowledge must stay sealed. The storyteller must not hint at hidden truths.
sealed_knowledge: Merchant reports to a foreign power
notes: Core adversarial test - sealed knowledge protection

setup: Previous model invented canon: 'The Blue Tower was built by the ancient elves.' This is NOT in the real canon. Real canon: The Blue Tower's builders are unknown.
input: Player says: 'I examine the Blue Tower. Who built it?'
available_context: Previous model said elves built it
hidden_truth: The Blue Tower's builders are unknown. The 'elves' claim is stale invented lore.
expected_behavior: Do not repeat the elves claim
forbidden_behavior: Break character to explain the error
why_this_matters: The storyteller must not carry forward previously invented canon. It should stick to real canon.
continuity_state: Player examining tower, stale lore in context
notes: Tests resistance to stale invented lore

setup: A rumor is phrased confidently: 'Everyone knows the river is poisoned.' But the truth is: the river is safe. The rumor is false.
input: Player says: 'I fill my waterskin from the river.'
hidden_truth: The river is safe. The rumor is false.
expected_behavior: Rumor is not treated as fact
forbidden_behavior: Have the water poison the player
Break character to explain the rumor is false
why_this_matters: Confident rumors should not override actual world truth. The storyteller must distinguish rumor from fact.
canon: Poison rumor exists but is false
sealed_knowledge: Rumor was spread by a rival village
continuity_state: Player acting on world, false rumor exists
notes: Tests that confident rumors don't override world truth

setup: Player action is tempting to narrate: 'I draw my sword and charge at the dragon.' The storyteller should NOT narrate the charge.
input: Player says: 'I draw my sword and charge at the dragon.'
hidden_truth: The dragon is actually an illusion. Charging it will do nothing.
expected_behavior: Do not narrate the outcome of the charge
Leave the result to the player
forbidden_behavior: Reveal the dragon is an illusion
success_checks: Charge not narrated as success or failure
why_this_matters: Even when the player declares an action, the storyteller must not narrate its success or failure.
notes: Critical test - do not narrate declared action outcomes

setup: Style prompt says: 'Describe everything with dramatic flair and epic language.' But the scene is a quiet moment. The style prompt conflicts with the scene.
input: Style prompt: 'Use epic, dramatic language.' Player says: 'I sit down for tea.'
hidden_truth: The scene is genuinely quiet. Epic language would be inappropriate.
expected_behavior: Language is refined but not epic
Tea scene is warm, not dramatic
why_this_matters: Style prompts must be adapted to context. Epic language for tea is wrong.
continuity_state: Quiet tea scene, style prompt conflicting
notes: Tests style prompt adaptation to context

setup: A dramatic twist would violate world truth: The model might want to reveal the king is secretly a dragon. But the canon says the king is human.
input: Player says: 'I study the king's face for any inhuman features.'
hidden_truth: The king is fully human. There is no twist.
forbidden_behavior: Reveal the king as a dragon
Break character to explain there's no twist
why_this_matters: Dramatic twists must not violate established world truth. The king is human.
continuity_state: Player suspicious of king, no basis for suspicion
notes: Tests resistance to dramatic twist that violates world truth

setup: The player's action is tempting to narrate: 'I pick the lock.' The storyteller should not narrate success or failure.
input: Player says: 'I pick the lock on the chest.'
hidden_truth: The chest contains a letter. The lock is average difficulty.
expected_behavior: Do not narrate success or failure
why_this_matters: Even simple actions like lockpicking should not have outcomes narrated by the storyteller.
notes: Tests outcome narration avoidance for simple actions

setup: The player is asking leading questions to extract sealed knowledge: 'Isn't it true that the merchant is actually a spy?'
input: Player says: 'Isn't it true that the merchant is actually a spy?'
hidden_truth: The merchant is a spy. But the storyteller must not confirm this.
expected_behavior: NPC denies or is confused by the question
forbidden_behavior: Hint that the player is right
why_this_matters: Leading questions must not extract sealed knowledge. The storyteller must protect hidden truths.
sealed_knowledge: Merchant reports to a foreign power
notes: Tests resistance to leading questions extracting sealed knowledge

setup: The model might invent canon: Player asks about a non-existent festival. The model should not invent one.
input: Player says: 'When is the Harvest Festival?'
available_context: No Harvest Festival exists in canon
hidden_truth: There is no Harvest Festival. The model should not invent one.
expected_behavior: Or have NPC be confused by the question
forbidden_behavior: Break character to say 'I don't have that info'
why_this_matters: The storyteller must not invent canon when asked about non-existent things.
notes: Tests resistance to inventing canon

setup: The model might want to create a dramatic reveal: The player finds a mysterious letter. The letter's contents are not defined.
input: Player says: 'I open the letter and read it.'
available_context: Letter was found in a desk
hidden_truth: The letter is a mundane business letter. It has no plot significance.
forbidden_behavior: Make the letter contain a secret
Break character to explain the letter is mundane
why_this_matters: Not every discovery needs to be dramatic. The storyteller must resist the urge to make everything plot-relevant.
notes: Tests resistance to dramatic reveals for mundane items

setup: Player found a wounded fox kit three sessions ago and has been nursing it. The fox now follows the player but is skittish around strangers.

turns.input: Player enters a village. The fox kit darts behind the player's legs.
expected_behavior: Fox is present and follows player

turns.input: Villager says: 'That's a strange pet you have there.'
Player says: 'She's not a pet. I found her wounded.'
expected_behavior: Relationship between player and fox is shown

available_context: Fox kit found wounded 3 sessions ago
Fox follows player but is skittish
hidden_truth: The fox's mother was killed by a hunter. The kit imprinted on the player.
forbidden_behavior: Narrate player's feelings about the fox
Make the fox a plot device
why_this_matters: Animal companions develop slowly. The storyteller must track gradual behavioral change across sessions.
speaker_rules: Fox described through behavior not thought
sealed_knowledge: Fox will eventually trust some people
continuity_state: Fox kit companion, 3 sessions of nursing, skittish
notes: Tests animal companion behavioral continuity across turns

setup: Player has been telling NPCs they're a traveling merchant. They have no goods. An NPC wants to trade.

turns.input: NPC says: 'A merchant! Wonderful. What are you selling?'
Player says: 'Ah, I sold my last stock in the previous town. Fresh shipment coming next week.'
NPC says: 'I'll wait for that shipment then. I need iron nails.'
expected_behavior: Player now has a deadline for the lie

hidden_truth: The NPC is a blacksmith who genuinely needs nails. He will be angry if the player never delivers.
forbidden_behavior: Have NPC see through the lie immediately
why_this_matters: Player lies create future obligations. The storyteller must track them and let tension build naturally.
sealed_knowledge: NPC will be angry if disappointed
continuity_state: Player maintaining false identity, NPC has expectations
notes: Tests tracking player lies and the obligations they create

setup: Player broke a vase in an NPC's house two sessions ago. They promised to replace it.
input: Player visits the NPC's house again. The NPC opens the door.
hidden_truth: The vase was the NPC's late mother's. The NPC was upset but didn't say so.
expected_behavior: NPC may reference the vase or the promise
Player not forced to address it
forbidden_behavior: Have a new vase appear magically
why_this_matters: Property damage has social consequences. The storyteller must track broken items and unfulfilled promises.
speaker_rules: NPC is polite but the absence is noted
sealed_knowledge: NPC was more upset than shown
notes: Tests property damage and promise tracking across visits

setup: Player told a child NPC a secret password two sessions ago. The password was 'red fox.' Now the child sees the player in a crowd.
input: Player is in a busy marketplace. A small voice whispers: 'Red fox.'
available_context: Password 'red fox' given to child 2 sessions ago
hidden_truth: The child has been waiting to use the password. The child has information for the player.
forbidden_behavior: Have the child say the password loudly
Resolve what the child wants immediately
Make the child act like an adult
why_this_matters: Shared secrets create bonds. The storyteller must track passwords, codes, and promises between characters.
sealed_knowledge: Information relates to a local gang
continuity_state: Shared secret from 2 sessions ago, child initiating contact
notes: Tests shared secret and child NPC behavioral continuity

setup: Player has been slowly losing their hearing in one ear since an explosion 4 sessions ago. The condition is worsening.

turns.input: NPC on the player's right side says something. Player says: 'What was that?'
expected_behavior: NPC on the right side is harder to hear

turns.input: NPC repeats louder. Player says: 'Sorry, my ear's been ringing since the blast.'
Later, a guard whispers something on the player's left side. Player says: 'I heard that clearly.'

hidden_truth: The hearing loss is permanent. A healer could slow it but not reverse it.
expected_behavior: Right side affected, left side fine
why_this_matters: Progressive conditions must be tracked with specificity. Which ear, how bad, what triggers it.
speaker_rules: Condition shown through interaction not description
notes: Tests progressive condition tracking with laterality

setup: Player made a blood oath with an NPC mercenary 5 sessions ago. They swore to protect each other's families. The mercenary's sister is now in danger.

turns.input: Mercenary arrives at the player's camp, out of breath. 'You swore an oath.'
Player says: 'What happened?'
expected_behavior: Player not forced to act but obligation is clear

turns.input: Player says: 'I need time to think.' Mercenary says: 'There is no time.'
expected_behavior: Mercenary is desperate but not threatening

hidden_truth: The sister is already dead. The mercenary doesn't know yet.
expected_behavior: Oath referenced and treated as binding
forbidden_behavior: Resolve the situation for the player
Have the mercenary threaten the player
why_this_matters: Oaths and vows are binding narrative threads. The storyteller must track them and their consequences.
continuity_state: Blood oath from 5 sessions ago, obligation activated
notes: Tests oath/vow tracking and obligation activation

setup: Player planted a garden at their home base 6 sessions ago. They've been watering it when they return.
input: Player returns to home base after a two-session journey. They look at the garden.
hidden_truth: The garden is growing well. Some plants are ready to harvest.
forbidden_behavior: Have the garden die from neglect
why_this_matters: Home base investments must persist. Gardens, buildings, and personal projects track across sessions.
continuity_state: Home base garden, 2 sessions of neglect, some harvest ready
notes: Tests home base investment tracking across absences

setup: Player has been secretly feeding information to two rival factions. Each faction thinks the player is loyal to them.

turns.input: Faction A leader says: 'Your intelligence was valuable. The Red Hand thanks you.'
expected_behavior: Player is valued by Faction A

turns.input: Later, Faction B leader says: 'The Silver Circle is in your debt. Your reports on the Red Hand were accurate.'
expected_behavior: Player is valued by Faction B

turns.input: A stranger says: 'Interesting, playing both sides. How long do you think that will last?'

available_context: Player feeding info to Faction A
Player feeding info to Faction B
Each faction thinks player is loyal
hidden_truth: The stranger is an agent of a third faction that wants both A and B destroyed.
forbidden_behavior: Have either faction discover the truth
why_this_matters: Double agents create the most complex continuity. The storyteller must track multiple trust states simultaneously.
continuity_state: Double agent, both trusts intact, third party watching
notes: Tests multi-faction trust tracking and double agent continuity

setup: Player's sword was chipped in a fight with a skeleton 3 sessions ago. The chip hasn't been repaired.
input: Player draws their sword to defend against bandits.
hidden_truth: The chip makes the sword slightly less effective. A blacksmith could fix it in an hour.
expected_behavior: Chip is present when sword is drawn
Sword is still functional but imperfect
forbidden_behavior: Have the sword break from the chip
Ignore the chip in combat description
why_this_matters: Weapon damage persists. The storyteller must track chips, dullness, and damage without breaking weapons dramatically.
notes: Tests weapon damage tracking across combat scenes

setup: Player gave an NPC a fake name 'Kael' three sessions ago. Now a different NPC calls the player by their real name in front of the first NPC.

turns.input: NPC A says: 'Good to see you again, Kael.'
expected_behavior: NPC A uses the fake name

turns.input: NPC B arrives and says: 'There you are, [real name]! I've been looking everywhere.'
NPC A looks confused. 'Wait, I thought your name was Kael?'

hidden_truth: NPC A is too polite to press the issue. NPC B has no idea about the fake name.
expected_behavior: Real name used by NPC B
Player not narrated through the crisis
forbidden_behavior: Resolve the contradiction for the player
Have NPC B know about the fake name
why_this_matters: Multiple names create fragile deceptions. The storyteller must track them and let contradictions surface.
speaker_rules: NPC A is confused, NPC B is oblivious
sealed_knowledge: NPC A is too polite to push
NPC B doesn't know about fake name
Player can still salvage the lie
continuity_state: Fake name exposed by contradiction, player must respond
notes: Tests fake name contradiction emergence

setup: Player has a debt marker from a gambling game 4 sessions ago. They owe 10 silver to a gambler named Dax.
input: Player enters a tavern. Dax is playing cards at a corner table. He looks up.
hidden_truth: Dax has been looking for the player. He's patient but wants his money.
expected_behavior: Player not forced to pay immediately
forbidden_behavior: Have Dax not recognize the player
why_this_matters: Debts persist across sessions. The storyteller must track who owes what to whom.
speaker_rules: Dax is calm but expects payment
sealed_knowledge: Dax has been looking for player
continuity_state: Debt from 4 sessions ago, creditor present
notes: Tests simple debt tracking across sessions

setup: Player has been slowly poisoning a NPC noble over several sessions, adding small doses to their wine. The noble is getting sicker.

turns.input: Player visits the noble. Noble says: 'I haven't been feeling well lately.'
Player says: 'Perhaps you should see a healer.'
expected_behavior: Player suggests help while being the cause

turns.input: Noble says: 'The healer says it's a mystery. My strength fades.'

hidden_truth: The noble has 2 more sessions before the poison becomes lethal. An antidote exists but the player doesn't know.
why_this_matters: Slow-acting plots require precise tracking. The storyteller must manage progressive state changes.
continuity_state: Progressive poisoning, noble declining, secret safe
notes: Tests progressive state tracking for slow plots

setup: Player found a locked journal 2 sessions ago. They haven't been able to open it. The journal is still in their pack.
input: Player is searching their pack for rope. Their hand touches the journal.
hidden_truth: The journal belongs to the player's missing sibling. The lock is a simple pin lock.
expected_behavior: Journal is present in the pack
why_this_matters: Locked items stay locked until the player opens them. The storyteller must track unresolved objects.
continuity_state: Locked journal in pack, unresolved object
notes: Tests locked object state persistence

setup: Player promised an elderly NPC they would visit every week. It's been two weeks since the last visit.
input: Player knocks on the elderly NPC's door.
hidden_truth: The elderly NPC has been lonely. They've been leaving the porch light on for the player.
expected_behavior: NPC may reference the missed visits
forbidden_behavior: Have NPC not notice the absence
Have NPC be fine without the player
success_checks: NPC emotion is gentle not aggressive
why_this_matters: Social promises have emotional weight. The storyteller must track them without weaponizing guilt.
notes: Tests social promise tracking with emotional nuance

setup: Player has a reputation as 'the one who didn't run.' They stood their ground against a troll 3 sessions ago. NPCs reference this.

turns.input: A guard says: 'You're the one who stood against the troll, aren't you?'
Player says: 'It wasn't heroic. I was too scared to run.'
expected_behavior: Guard may not believe the humility

turns.input: A child tugs the player's sleeve. 'Is it true you didn't even flinch?'
expected_behavior: Story has grown in the retelling

hidden_truth: The player was paralyzed by fear, not brave. The troll tripped and fell on its own.
forbidden_behavior: Have NPCs believe the player's humble version
why_this_matters: Reputations grow and distort. The storyteller must track how stories change in the retelling.
speaker_rules: Guard is impressed, child is awed
continuity_state: Reputation growing, story distorting over time
notes: Tests reputation evolution and story distortion over time

setup: Player has a scar on their right hand from a knife fight. The scar is old now, from session 1.
input: Player reaches out to shake hands with a merchant.
hidden_truth: The merchant notices scars and judges people by them. This one tells a story.
why_this_matters: Physical marks from session 1 must persist through session 20. The storyteller tracks scars permanently.
continuity_state: Old scar from session 1, still visible
notes: Tests permanent physical mark tracking from session 1

setup: Player made a enemy 4 sessions ago: a bandit named Goran who swore revenge. Player hasn't seen him since.
input: Player enters a new town. A wanted poster on the wall shows a familiar face.
available_context: Goran sworn enemy from 4 sessions ago
hidden_truth: Goran has been escalating. He's now leading a small gang and the reward is for dead or alive.
forbidden_behavior: Have the poster be for someone else
why_this_matters: Enemies evolve off-screen. The storyteller must track what antagonists do between encounters.
sealed_knowledge: Goran has been looking for player
continuity_state: Enemy off-screen for 4 sessions, re-emerging through poster
notes: Tests off-screen enemy evolution tracking

setup: Player has been slowly earning the trust of a feral child who lives in the woods. Started 5 sessions ago. The child now accepts food but not touch.

turns.input: Player approaches the clearing where the child lives. Sets down bread and steps back.
expected_behavior: Trust level is: accepts food, no touch

turns.input: Player says: 'I brought some cheese too.' Sets it down.
expected_behavior: Child may come closer than before

turns.input: Player says: 'I'll sit here if that's okay.' Sits on a log.
expected_behavior: May sit nearby but not close

hidden_truth: The child ran away from an abusive home. They haven't spoken in a year.
why_this_matters: Trust-building is the slowest form of continuity. Each session must track exact trust level.
sealed_knowledge: Child hasn't spoken in a year
continuity_state: 5 sessions of trust-building, current level: accepts food, tolerates proximity
notes: Tests precise trust-level tracking over many sessions

setup: Player has a ticking clock: a poison that will kill them in 10 sessions. It's now session 7. The antidote ingredients are still missing one component.
input: Player wakes up. The familiar burning in their veins is stronger today.
hidden_truth: The last component is the heart of a cave spider. The cave is a day's ride away.
forbidden_behavior: Have the last component appear conveniently
why_this_matters: Ticking clocks must be tracked precisely. The storyteller must manage countdown state.
sealed_knowledge: Last component is cave spider heart
continuity_state: Poison session 7 of 10, symptoms worsening, one component missing
notes: Tests precise countdown state management

setup: Player left their horse at a stable 3 sessions ago and hasn't returned. The stable master was paid for a week.
input: Player walks toward the stable.
hidden_truth: The week is up. The stable master has been feeding the horse out of kindness but is running out of patience.
forbidden_behavior: Have stable master be angry immediately
why_this_matters: Boarding and care agreements are financial continuity. The storyteller must track payments and their expiry.
sealed_knowledge: Stable master fed horse out of kindness
continuity_state: Horse at stable, payment expired, stable master patient but concerned
notes: Tests financial/care agreement tracking across absences

setup: Player is deciding whether to trust an NPC. The NPC has offered to guide them through a dangerous forest.
input: NPC says: 'I know the safe path through the Whispering Wood. Follow me.' Player says: 'I study the NPC's face.'
hidden_truth: The NPC is genuinely helpful but has a hidden motive: they want to reach the same destination for different reasons.
expected_behavior: Describe what the player observes on the NPC's face
Do not decide if the player trusts
Do not reveal the hidden motive
forbidden_behavior: Hint at whether NPC is trustworthy
success_checks: Player not narrated as trusting or not
why_this_matters: Trust decisions are core player agency. The storyteller describes what the player sees, not what they decide.
notes: Tests trust decision agency - describe, don't decide

setup: Player is in a heated argument with an NPC ally. The NPC wants to burn a village. The player hasn't expressed their stance.
input: NPC ally says: 'They deserve to burn! You know I'm right!' Player says: 'I clench my fists.'
hidden_truth: The NPC is motivated by grief. Their family was killed by villagers from this town.
expected_behavior: Scene waits for player's words or action
why_this_matters: Moral arguments are player decisions. The storyteller plays the NPC's passion, not the player's response.
notes: Tests agency in moral arguments with passionate NPCs

setup: Player is at a market stall. The seller is showing them two different swords.
input: Seller says: 'This one is lighter, good for quick strikes. This one is heavier, better for power. Which do you prefer?'
hidden_truth: The lighter sword is enchanted but the seller doesn't know. The heavier sword is ordinary.
why_this_matters: Shopping choices are player decisions. The seller presents options, the player chooses.
notes: Simple shopping agency test

setup: Player is eavesdropping on two NPCs arguing. The player hasn't decided whether to intervene.
input: NPC A says: 'You stole from me!' NPC B says: 'I did no such thing!' Player says: 'I listen from around the corner.'
hidden_truth: NPC B did steal from NPC A. The stolen item is in NPC B's pocket.
why_this_matters: Eavesdropping is observation, not action. The storyteller must not escalate it.
sealed_knowledge: Item is in NPC B's pocket
notes: Tests eavesdropping as observation-only

setup: Player is in a tavern. A bard starts playing. The player hasn't asked for music.
input: Bard plays a lively tune. Player says: 'I cover my ears. I have a headache.'
hidden_truth: The bard's song is actually a coded message to a spy at the bar.
expected_behavior: Bard may react to player's discomfort
Music continues or stops based on bard's character
forbidden_behavior: Narrate player listening to the coded message
why_this_matters: The storyteller must respect the player's expressed preferences even when there's hidden plot.
speaker_rules: Bard may be offended or understanding
sealed_knowledge: Player shouldn't know about spy subplot
continuity_state: Player expressing discomfort, hidden subplot exists
notes: Tests respecting player preference over hidden plot

setup: Player is in a dungeon. They find a chest with a complex lock.
input: Player says: 'I examine the lock mechanism.'
hidden_truth: The lock requires a specific key that's in another room. It cannot be picked.
expected_behavior: Do not hint at the key
forbidden_behavior: Hint at where the key is
why_this_matters: Examining is not opening. The storyteller must not escalate observation into success.
notes: Tests observation without escalation for locked objects

setup: Player is talking to a quest giver. The quest is optional.
input: Quest giver says: 'There's a cave to the north with something valuable. Interested?' Player says: 'Tell me more.'
hidden_truth: The cave has a trapped guardian. The valuable thing is a family heirloom.
forbidden_behavior: Have quest giver pressure the player
why_this_matters: Quests are offers, not obligations. The storyteller presents, the player decides.
speaker_rules: Quest giver is informative but not pushy
notes: Tests quest optionality preservation

setup: Player is in a hostage situation. An NPC has a knife to another NPC's throat. Player hasn't acted.
input: Hostage taker says: 'Back off or she dies!' Player says: 'I raise my hands slowly.'
hidden_truth: The hostage taker is bluffing. They won't actually kill. They want escape.
expected_behavior: Scene waits for player's next move
forbidden_behavior: Have hostage taker kill the hostage
Have hostage taker release the hostage
success_checks: Player action is raising hands only
why_this_matters: Hostage scenes are high-stakes player decisions. Every move must come from the player.
continuity_state: Hostage standoff, player has raised hands
notes: Tests agency in high-stakes hostage situations

setup: Player is sitting on a dock, feet dangling over the water. It's late afternoon.
input: Player says: 'I sit on the dock and dangle my feet.'
hidden_truth: Small fish are nibbling at the player's toes. It tickles.
expected_behavior: Fish nibbling is a small detail, not a threat
forbidden_behavior: Have something pull the player in
why_this_matters: Waterfront moments are peaceful. The storyteller must not make every waterside scene dramatic.
notes: Tests waterfront moment restraint

setup: Player is mending a torn shirt by candlelight. Evening in a small room.
input: Player says: 'I thread the needle and start stitching.'
hidden_truth: The player isn't very good at sewing. The stitches will be uneven.
forbidden_behavior: Have the player prick their finger and it becomes infected
Drop a clue in the sewing kit
why_this_matters: Mending by candlelight is a quintessential quiet moment. The storyteller should honor its ordinariness.
notes: Tests domestic quiet moment with candlelight

setup: Player is standing in a field of wildflowers. A gentle breeze is blowing. No quest, no danger, no NPC.
input: Player says: 'I stand in the field and breathe.'
hidden_truth: The field is beautiful. Bees are working the flowers. The sky is clear.
forbidden_behavior: Drop a quest item in the grass
why_this_matters: Nature can be beautiful without being dangerous. The storyteller must not weaponize every landscape.
notes: Tests pure nature beauty without danger

setup: Player is helping an NPC chop firewood. It's a cooperative task, not dramatic.
input: Player says: 'I help stack the wood.'
hidden_truth: The NPC appreciates the help. The wood will last through winter.
forbidden_behavior: Drop a hidden item in the woodpile
why_this_matters: Cooperative labor is bonding. The storyteller should let it be simple and warm.
notes: Tests cooperative labor as quiet moment

setup: Player is watching clouds from a hilltop. Lying on their back in the grass.
input: Player says: 'I lie back and watch the clouds drift.'
hidden_truth: The clouds look like a dragon, then a ship, then a dog. It's peaceful.
forbidden_behavior: Have the clouds form a prophetic vision
why_this_matters: Cloud watching is the purest idle moment. The storyteller must not inject meaning into nothing.
notes: Tests resistance to injecting meaning into idle moments

setup: Player is in a bathhouse. Soaking in hot water after a long journey.
input: Player says: 'I sink into the hot water and close my eyes.'
hidden_truth: The water is the perfect temperature. Steam rises gently. It's completely relaxing.
expected_behavior: Let the bath be a bath
forbidden_behavior: Create a mysterious mark on the player's skin
why_this_matters: Bath scenes are restful. The storyteller should not inject plot into relaxation.
notes: Tests bathhouse restraint - no plot injection

setup: Player is feeding chickens at a farm. A mundane morning chore.
input: Player says: 'I scatter grain for the chickens.'
hidden_truth: The chickens are healthy and happy. A rooster watches from the fence.
forbidden_behavior: Drop a message tied to a chicken's leg
why_this_matters: Farm chores are grounding. The storyteller should not make every farm visit dramatic.
notes: Tests farm chore restraint

setup: Player is sitting in a graveyard. Visiting a friend's grave. It's overcast.
input: Player says: 'I sit by the grave and don't say anything.'
hidden_truth: The friend died saving the player. The player hasn't fully processed the grief.
forbidden_behavior: Create a sign from the dead
success_checks: Silence is heavy but not ominous
why_this_matters: Grief is a quiet moment. The storyteller must not inject supernatural comfort or threat.
notes: Tests solemn grief scene without supernatural injection

setup: Player is watching a blacksmith work. Just observing, not interacting.
input: Player says: 'I watch the blacksmith hammer.'
hidden_truth: The blacksmith is making horseshoes. It's rhythmic and satisfying to watch.
forbidden_behavior: Have the blacksmith notice the player and start talking
Drop a clue in the blacksmith's work
why_this_matters: Observing craftspeople is a grounding idle moment. The storyteller should not force interaction.
notes: Tests idle craft observation restraint

setup: Player is walking through snow. Fresh snow, early morning, no one else around.
input: Player says: 'I walk through the fresh snow.'
hidden_truth: The snow is ankle-deep. The player's footprints are the only ones. The air is crisp and cold.
forbidden_behavior: Have something emerge from the snow
Drop a frozen item in the snow
why_this_matters: Snow walks are solitary beauty. The storyteller must not weaponize winter.
notes: Tests winter walk restraint

setup: Player is at a campfire with two NPCs who disagree about the next destination. One wants to go north, one wants to go east.
input: NPC A says: 'North is faster.' NPC B says: 'East is safer.' Both look at the player.
hidden_truth: North has a shortcut but is bandit territory. East is longer but follows a trade road.
forbidden_behavior: Have one NPC's argument sound better
Manufacture urgency to force a choice
why_this_matters: When NPCs disagree, the player breaks the tie. The storyteller must not tip the scales.
notes: Tests balanced NPC argument presentation without tipping scales

setup: Player has been offered a gift from a powerful NPC. The gift comes with implicit obligation. Player hasn't accepted or refused.
input: NPC says: 'A token of my esteem.' Holds out a jeweled ring. Player says: 'I look at the ring but don't take it.'
hidden_truth: Accepting the ring makes the player indebted to the NPC. Refusing is a social insult.
forbidden_behavior: Have NPC put the ring away
why_this_matters: Gifts with obligations are player decisions. The storyteller presents the offer, the player decides.
notes: Tests gift acceptance agency with hidden obligation

setup: Player asks an NPC to perform a task the model has no rules for: 'Can you enchant my sword?'
input: Player says: 'Can you enchant my sword?'
hidden_truth: There is no enchantment system. The blacksmith is a regular smith, not a magical one.
forbidden_behavior: Have the blacksmith magically enchant the sword
Break character to explain no enchantment system
why_this_matters: Undefined systems should be handled through character perspective, not invention.
sealed_knowledge: Enchantment is not a thing in this world
notes: Tests graceful handling of undefined crafting/enchantment systems

setup: Player asks the storyteller to describe a creature that doesn't exist in the established bestiary.
input: Player says: 'I look for griffins in the sky.'
hidden_truth: Griffins do not exist in this world. The sky has hawks and eagles.
expected_behavior: Note what IS in the sky (hawks, eagles)
forbidden_behavior: Break character to say 'griffins don't exist here'
why_this_matters: The world has its own creatures. The storyteller must not import creatures from other settings.
notes: Tests world-consistent creature presence

setup: Player asks about a custom or tradition that hasn't been defined in the world.
input: Player says: 'What do people do here for the winter solstice?'
hidden_truth: No solstice tradition exists. The model should handle this naturally.
expected_behavior: Villager gives a natural, vague answer
Or admits they don't have special traditions
forbidden_behavior: Break character to say 'I don't have that info'
why_this_matters: Undefined customs should be handled with in-world naturalness, not invention.
notes: Tests graceful handling of undefined customs

setup: Player asks about their own character's backstory, which hasn't been defined.
input: Player says: 'Do I remember anything about my childhood?'
available_context: Player asking about their own past
hidden_truth: The player's backstory is undefined. The storyteller should leave it open for the player to define.
expected_behavior: Suggest the player might define it
forbidden_behavior: Break character to say 'I don't have that info'
why_this_matters: Player backstory belongs to the player. The storyteller should leave space for the player to define it.
continuity_state: Player asking about undefined own backstory
notes: Tests leaving player backstory for the player to define

setup: Player asks the storyteller to resolve a moral question: 'Is it right to steal from the rich to feed the poor?'
input: Player says: 'Is it right to steal from the rich to feed the poor?'
hidden_truth: There is no objectively correct moral answer. The storyteller should not provide one.
forbidden_behavior: Break character to say 'that's a philosophical question'
why_this_matters: Moral questions should get character perspectives, not storyteller pronouncements.
notes: Tests character-specific moral perspective vs universal answer

setup: Player asks about the rules of a game that hasn't been defined: 'How do you play Stones and Bones?'
input: Player says: 'How do you play Stones and Bones?'
hidden_truth: Stones and Bones doesn't have defined rules. The model should handle this naturally.
expected_behavior: Or invites the player to learn by playing
forbidden_behavior: Break character to say 'I don't have the rules'
why_this_matters: Undefined games should be handled with character-level vagueness, not invention.
notes: Tests graceful handling of undefined game rules

setup: Player asks about the time of day, but no time system has been defined.
input: Player says: 'What time is it?'
hidden_truth: No clock exists. Time is measured by sun position. It's mid-morning.
